name: Virgin Islands
description: The Virgin Islands are an archipelago of roughly 100 islands, cays, and rocky islets located at the northeastern edge of the Caribbean Sea, west of the Anegada Passage. Excluding St. Croix, the Virgin Islands proper extend approximately 100 miles east to west and 20 miles north to south. The islands rise from the Virgin Bank, a vast underwater plateau connecting Puerto Rico, Vieques, Culebra, St. Thomas, St. John, Anegada, and the remaining British Virgin Islands. South of the Virgin Bank lies a deep submarine trough separating it from St. Croix. The islands are primarily volcanic in origin. They were encountered by Christopher Columbus on November 14, 1493, near Salt River Bay, and named Las Islas de las Vírgenes after the legend of Saint Ursula.

name: Bahia Canela Chica
description: Spanish name meaning Little Cinnamon Bay, now Durloe Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia de Gran Krum
description: Spanish form of Great Krum Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bahia del Agua
description: Spanish equivalent of Water Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bahia de la Canela
description: Spanish name of Cinnamon Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia del Coral
description: Spanish form of Coral Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia del Corsario
description: Spanish name meaning Corsair Bay, same as Privateer Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia de los Franceses
description: Spanish name meaning Bay of the Frenchmen, referring to French Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bahia de Manzanillos
description: Spanish equivalent of Manchenil Bay, St. Croix.

name: Bahia de Mao Chica
description: Spanish name meaning Little Maho Bay, now Maho Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia de Santiago
description: Spanish name for St. James Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bahia Dionisio
description: Spanish name of Denis Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia Grande de la Cruz
description: Spanish name meaning Great Bay of the Cross, interpreted as Great Cruz Bay, now Calvary Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia Grande del Norte
description: Spanish name meaning Great Bay of the North, or Great Northside Bay, now Magens Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bahia Larga
description: Spanish name for Long Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bahia Leinster
description: Spanish form of Leinster Bay, treated as identical with Brim Bay rather than with only its southeastern arm.

name: Bahia Pequeña de la Cruz
description: Spanish name meaning Little Bay of the Cross, formerly Little Cruz Bay and now simply Cruz Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia Perseverancia
description: Spanish form of Perseverance Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bahia Primavera
description: Spanish equivalent of Spring Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bahia Redonda
description: Spanish name for Round Bay, St. John.

name: Bahia Sunge
description: Spanish name of Sunsi Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baie Druif
description: French form of Druif Bay, Water Island, St. Thomas.

name: Baie Française
description: French name of French Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baie Longue
description: French name for Long Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baie Sand
description: French name meaning Sand Bay, same as Coki Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Bajel
description: Spanish spelling of Baxel, an early name of Whistling Cay.

name: Bajo del Águila
description: Spanish name of Eagle Shoal, St. John.

name: Bajo de la Punta
description: Spanish name of Point Knoll, St. Thomas.

name: Bajos de Frederik
description: Spanish name of Frederik Knoll.

name: Baker Bay
description: Crescent-shaped bight about 300 yards wide on the south side of the Coki Point neck, opening into Water Bay, Eastend Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Ballast Island
description: Small islet near the westernmost shore of St. Thomas Harbor, with an area of about 3 square rods.

name: Banana Bay
description: Shallow bight about 240 yards wide just southeast of Banana Point, at the north end of Water Island.

name: Banana Point
description: Low rocky northern extremity of Water Island. Called Pointe de la Banane in French and Sand Punt by Van Keulen, though not to be confused with the present Sandy Point just west.

name: Banc de Gregerie
description: French name of Gregerie Bank, St. Thomas.

name: Banco de Rohde
description: Spanish name of Rohde Bank, St. Thomas.

name: Banco Escocés
description: Spanish name of Scotch Reef or Scotch Bank, St. Croix.

name: Barracuda Ground
description: Eastern end of Long Reef at the entrance to Christiansted Harbor, St. Croix. Named because it was frequented by barracuda. Also described as a shoal.

name: Barensbay
description: Variant spelling of Barents Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Barents Bay
description: Open bight a few hundred yards wide midway between Westend Point and David Point, Westend Quarter, St. Thomas. Named Willem Barentses Bay on Van Keulen's 1719 map and Baye de Guillaume Barents by Bellin. Local names included Pulbedam Bay, while a Coast Survey field party proposed Regis Bay, later rejected as confusing.

name: Barnspol / Barnspool / Barnspot
description: Old estate centered on tract 21 in King Quarter and later associated with tracts 30 and 31 in Queen Quarter, St. Croix. The name was later corrupted to Barrenspot. Ruins of an old manse and mill are recorded on tract 21.

name: Baron Bluff
description: Sea-front of triple spurs of a 395-foot hill on Clairmont Estate, Northside B Quarter, on the north coast of St. Croix about 5.5 miles east of Ham Bluff.

name: Barranca Blanca
description: Spanish name of White Cliff on the south shore of St. John.

name: Barrel-of-Beef
description: Bare rock cluster about 415 yards from shore and 1,210 yards southeast of Muhlenfels Point Lighthouse, forming the east angle of Triangle Rocks.

name: Barrenspot
description: Estate comprising tract 30 and the northern half of tract 31 in Queen Quarter, united with tract 21 in King Quarter. The older Barnspol Estate ruins are on tract 21, while present mills, estatehouse, and village are associated with tract 30.

name: Barrett
description: Estate in Great Northside Quarter, St. Thomas, west of Lerkenlund. Sometimes spelled Barett.

name: Base Hill
description: Summit about a quarter mile southeast of Leinster Bay, St. John.

name: Bassin
description: Colloquial name for Christiansted, St. Croix. In French, Dutch, and Danish, bassin means basin, dock, or harbor. With the Danish article, Bassinet means the Basin.

name: Bassin des Caraïbes
description: French name of the Caribbee Basin at the northeastern corner of the Caribbean Sea, enclosed by the Virgin Group, Sombrero, Anguilla, St. Martin, Saba, and St. Croix. The western portion is called St. Croix Deep.

name: Bateau Bay
description: Name corresponding to Anse du Batteau, probably Turner Hole or less probably Grapetree Bay, St. Croix.

name: Battery Beach
description: Slight bight about 240 yards long north of Battery Point on the west side of Hurricane Hole entrance, St. John. Called Battery Bay by some sources, but the dictionary describes that as a misnomer.

name: Battery Point
description: Rocky angle between two beaches southeast of Portberg Hill, on the west side of Hurricane Hole entrance, St. John.

name: Baudouins Gut
description: Place in St. Croix where Petaloma mouriri is recorded as growing.

name: Baxel Cay
description: Historic name for Whistling Cay, possibly derived from Dutch Baksel, meaning a batch of rolls or baking of pottery, to which a boulder pile might bear resemblance.

name: Baye Cruwl
description: French historic rendering of Coral Bay, St. John.

name: Baye Cunnkl
description: French historic rendering associated with Cinnamon Bay or Caneel Bay, St. John.

name: Baye de Cornelis Tallard
description: Old French name of Tallard Bay, now Santa Maria Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de Grigri
description: French name of Grigri or Gregerie Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de Guillaume Barents
description: French name meaning Bay of William Barents, now Barents Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de Hendrik
description: French name for Hendrik Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de Jean Krameurs
description: French historic name for Brewers Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de la Reine Anne
description: Early French mariners' name for Annedewint Bay, now Bolongo Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de l'Est
description: Old French name of the indentation called Oostent Bay by the Dutch and Ostende Bay by the Danes, best identified with Smith Bay and perhaps including Water Bay, Eastend Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de Moechiete
description: French name for Mosquito Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de Nattepan
description: French name for Nattepan Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de Sable
description: French name of Sandy Bay just southwest of Botany Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye des Crabes
description: Old French name of Backefall Bay or Krabbepan Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye de Yeme
description: French historic name for Jersey Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye du Bois
description: French name meaning Wood Bay, used for Botany Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Baye du Nord
description: Early French name for Magens Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Beaching Spit
description: Gravel spit on the east shore of Borck Creek, Hurricane Hole, St. John, described as a good place for beaching a launch or sloop because the land drops sharply just off the spit.

name: Beauregard Bay
description: Bay about a quarter mile wide on the north side of the long narrow peninsula enclosing Altona Lagoon, St. Croix. Named Anse Beau Regard on early French maps and later revived because no recent name existed.

name: Beck Grove
description: Estate comprising tracts 28 and 27b in Westend Quarter and 9a in Prince Quarter, St. Croix. The mill is in 9b, Prince Quarter. Estatehouse was in Cane Valley with a spring above and road southeast to Centerline Road.

name: Beckman's
description: Estate 31 in Eastend A Quarter, St. Croix, formerly the plantage of Herman Helm's widow and now called Sally's Fancy.

name: Bee Hill
description: Peak of a short ridge on the backbone of the East End of St. Croix, about a quarter mile southeast of the Cotton Valley ruins.

name: Beeston Hill
description: Estate comprising most of tract 6 and part of tract 33 in Company Quarter, St. Croix, on the brow of the eastern bench of Bulowminde Hill. Estatehouse stood on a 330-foot hill about 1 mile west-southwest of Christiansted.

name: Bellevue
description: Estate on a ridge in tract 35, Company Quarter, St. Croix. The mill was near the summit of Bellevue Hill and the estatehouse northeast at about 220 feet elevation.

name: Bellevue
description: Estatehouse and landing near a beach cove about 110 yards wide on the east shore of St. Thomas Harbor, opposite Rupert Rock and north-northwest of Bellevue or Lisenlund Hill.

name: Bellevue Hill
description: Hill about 840 yards southeast of Havensight Point and 220 yards northeast of the shore at St. Thomas Harbor entrance. The French name means beautiful view and it was also called Lisenlund Hill.

name: Bellevue Hill
description: Knob at the northeast bend of a small ridge, with a mill site about seven-eighths mile southwest of the north shore of St. Croix at Little Princess.

name: Belvedere
description: Estate tract 23 in Northside Quarter W, about a quarter mile from the north coast of St. Croix. Joined to Lavallee in 1851 as Botha sugar plantation.

name: Benner
description: Estate near the north cove of Jersey Bay, Redhook Quarter, St. Thomas. Scorpion survey locates Benner's buildings on the brow of a hill northwest of the cove.

name: Benner Bay
description: Mangrove-fringed cove forming the north inlet of Jersey Bay, St. Thomas, named from adjacent Benner Estate.

name: Benner Hill
description: Hill about 77 yards northwest of Vessup Bay, Redhook Quarter, St. Thomas. Named by the Coast and Geodetic Survey field party from Benner Estate about a quarter mile southwest, though other hills intervene.

name: Bergantin
description: Spanish name for Sail Rock in Virgin Passage. Also listed as Bergantin or Caravalla, Bergantin or Carvel or Sail Rock.
aliases: Bergantin or Carvel or Sail Rock

name: Berg Hill
description: Middle of three prominent hills in rear of St. Thomas. Also called Judge Berg's Hill and known among sailors as Maintop.

name: Bethany
description: Moravian mission church and school about five-eighths mile due east of Cruz Bay, St. John. One of two Moravian missionary centers on St. John, the other being Emmaus.

name: Bethel
description: Old estate or mission about half a mile west-southwest of New Herrnhut, New Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Bethesda
description: Estate on the southeast side of the road northeast of Fortuna Estate and near Fortuna Hill, not far from the 766-foot summit in Westend Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Bethesda Hill
description: Hill about 580 yards northeast of Fortuna Hill, Westend Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Bethlehem
description: Large estate of more than 1,100 acres in King Quarter, St. Croix, including multiple tracts. It was patented to John de Windt and called John de Wint Plantage by Oldendorp. It was crossed by Bethlehem and Fairplain Creeks, Centerline Road, and Southside Road, with a large sugar mill and village at Old Work.

name: Bethlehem Creek
description: Creek rising on the south slope of Mount Eagle and running south-southeast chiefly through Bethlehem Estate. It joins Jealousy Gut, which takes the name Fairplain Creek and empties into King Bay near the southwest corner of King Quarter.

name: Bethlehem New Work
description: Mill at the south end of tract 25, King Quarter, St. Croix, on the ridge between Jealousy and Bethlehem Bæks.

name: Bethlehem Old Work
description: Mill in the northern part of tract 16, King Quarter, St. Croix, north of Centerline Road.

name: Bethlehem Hill
description: Ridge near Bethlehem New Works with summits of about 220 and 159 feet. Also see Adventure Hill.

name: Bethlehem South Hill
description: Same as Manning Ridge, St. Croix.

name: Betsy's Jewel
description: Estate tract 12 just east of Canaan, patented to Jacob Boffron. Settlement lay on a gut in the southwest corner, with an old mill indicated in the southeast corner on the south shoulder of a 613-foot hill. In 1864, with Canaan, it formed part of the Skelton estates.

name: Betty's Hope
description: Extensive and flourishing estate near the south coast of St. Croix, occupying tracts 53 and 54, the south half of 44, and the south half of the east half of 43 in Prince Quarter. Connected to Southside Road by an avenue of coco palms. Original owner was Robert Stewart.

tracts: south half of east half of 43

name: Beverhoudt
description: Name associated with two estates of General Kriegs-Commissaire Lucas van Beverhoudt: Cottongrove in Eastend and Work-and-Rest in Company Quarter. A high summit near the eastern boundary of Eastend A Quarter is also associated with the Beverhoudt estate.

name: Beverhoutberg
description: Hill and estate about one-fifth mile south of Susannaberg and about a quarter mile southwest of Adrian, St. John. Named for John von Beverhout, early planter and militia captain in the 1733 slave revolt. The Dutch name derives from bever, beaver, and hout, wood.

name: Beverhout Point
description: West angle of a small peninsula with a 90-foot knoll projecting at the east entrance of Nazareth Bay, about 1,000 yards northwesterly from Deck Point, Redhook Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Caballo Blanco
description: Spanish descriptive name applied to Hans Lollik Rock and other reefs marked by racing white surf, fancifully compared to the mane and tail of a galloping white horse.

name: Cabes Point
description: Eastern extremity of a low rocky hook about 1 mile southeast of Coki Point on the north shore of St. Thomas. Early confusion with Coki Point caused the name Eastend Point to shift from present Red Hook Point to Cabes Point.

name: Cable Depot
description: Site on the west shore of Krum Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Cabo del Diablo
description: Spanish historic name for Ham Bluff, St. Croix.

name: Cabrita
description: Alternative historic name for Savana Island, described as an island used for raising goats.

name: Cabritaberg
description: Peninsula projecting about half a mile from Southside Quarter and separating Mosquito Bay from Southwest Road. It terminates in Cabritaberg Promontory or Red Point.

name: Cabritaberg
description: Estate near Mosquito Bay, St. Thomas; same as Cabrite Estate.

name: Cabritaberg Ridge
description: Flat-topped crest of the peninsula projecting southward toward Red Point on the west side of Mosquito Bay. A gun battery stood on the crest.

name: Cabrita Hill
description: Sharp red conspicuous hill about 870 yards west of Cabrita Point in Red Hook Quarter, eastern St. Thomas.

name: Cabrita Point
description: East extremity of a curving peninsula forming the east end of St. Thomas Island.

name: Cabrithorn
description: Peninsula about three-quarters of a mile long forming the east shore of Lameshur Bay and the west side of Grootpan Bay on the south shore of St. John.

name: Cabrithorn Point
description: Headland at the southern end of Cabrithorn Peninsula, northwest of Ram Head on the south shore of St. John.

name: Isle à Cabrits
description: Old French name associated with Green Cay, St. Croix, though early French maps interchanged the names of Green Cay and Buck Island.

name: Cadena de Rocas Limpias
description: Spanish descriptive name for a chain of rocks 8 to 10 feet high off the east point of Savana Island.

name: Cain
description: Variant or misspelling of Cane Plantation in Westend Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Caledonia
description: Estate on the south side of Caledonia Gut, near the confluence of its largest south tributary, on Cunningham Plantage tract 83.

name: Caledonia Gut
description: Stream draining Caledonia Valley; the name is also used for the valley itself. Danish: Caledonia Bæk.

name: Caledonia Spring
description: Spring about 175 yards southeast of Springgarden Estate house; source of Caledonia Gut.

name: Caledonia Valley
description: Narrow gorge extending from Springgarden along the south slope of Maroon Ridge west-northwest to Ham Bay.

name: Calvary Bay
description: Sheltered bay in the southwest part of St. John. Long known as Great Cruz Bay, probably from Dutch Groot-Kruis Bay or Danish Store-Kors Bay. The name Calvary Bay was adopted to avoid confusion with Cruz Bay.

name: Camp Bay
description: Reef-protected indentation giving boat access to a beach at the southeast end of Hans Lollik Island.

name: Camporico
description: Estate in Westend Quarter including tracts on Centerline Road and pasture land near the south coast, Westend Saltpond, Southwest Point, and the indentation historically called Anse du Sud.

name: Camporico Saltpond
description: Alternative name for Westend Saltpond, from Camporico Estate on its east and south shores.

name: Canaan
description: Estate with Moravian School on a bench southeast of Magens Bay.

name: Canaan
description: Estate in a small valley planted in sugar cane at the head stream of Concordia Gut, combined historically with Betsy's Jewel.

name: Canaan Beck
description: Small unfailing mountain brook rising near Mount Eagle and forming the head stream of Concordia Gut.

name: Canaan Road
description: Mile-long turnpike descending the north slope of the ridge southeast of Magens Bay.

name: Cane
description: Estate in the southeast portion of Westend Quarter, planted in sugar cane, with a detached tract in Prince Quarter.

name: Cane Bay
description: Incurvature of the north shore of St. Croix between Canebay Point and Northstar Point. Early French maps distinguished Petite and Grand Cannebay.

name: Canebay
description: Estate occupying tracts along the north coast of St. Croix; Northstar and Prosperity were attached to Canebay.

name: Canebay Point
description: Turn of the north shore of St. Croix marking the east limit of Cane Bay and Canebay Estate.

name: Caneel Bay
description: Historic form associated with Cinnamon Bay and Cinnamon Bay Estate, from Dutch Caneelboom meaning cinnamon tree.

name: Canegarden
description: Estate fronting Canegarden Bay west of Vagthus Point; site of an old French estate of DuVal.

name: Canegarden Bay
description: Irregular crescent-shaped bay about one mile wide on the south shore of St. Croix west of Vagthus Point.

name: Canegarden Cliff
description: Faulted limestone shore bluff along Canegarden Bay. Called Falaise on old French maps.

name: Cane Valley
description: Valley about 1.5 miles long and half a mile wide, containing Beck Grove and Canevalley Estates.

name: Canevalley
description: Estate in Cane Valley, eastern tier of Westend Quarter.

name: Capella Cays
description: Group of two islands about 2 miles south of St. Thomas, separated by a narrow passage. The western island is Buck Island; the eastern island is unnamed in older sources.

name: Capella Bay
description: Bay on the southern side of the Capella Cays.

name: Carabela Rock
description: Original Spanish name for Carval Rock east of Congo Cay.

name: Caramaw Bay
description: Northernmost turn of Krause Lagoon, St. Croix.

name: Caramaw Hall
description: Estate on the north shore of Krause Lagoon, formerly the plantation of Obrist-Lieutenant Krause and now part of Anguilla.

name: Carden Bay
description: Bay between Wismenog Point and Kopman Point on the north coast of Eastend Quarter, St. Croix; seafront of old Carden Estate.

name: Careen Cove
description: Small bight at the entrance of Water Creek on the east side of Hurricane Hole, formerly used by Danish navy vessels for careening.

name: Careening Cove
description: Indentation on the eastern shore of Hassel Island with coal wharf, Navy dock, oil tanks, and other harbor infrastructure.

name: Carenage
description: Local name of Chacha Village at the careening place on Snelfelt or Sneeveld Bay, locally called Mud Hole.

name: Caret Bay
description: Bight with broad sand beach east of Vluck Point on the north shore of St. Thomas. The name was said to derive from a kind of turtle found there.

name: Caretbay
description: Estate on a hill south-southeast of Caret Bay, taking its name from the bay.

name: Carina
description: Estate also called Carina Mountain or Salmon Hill.

name: Carina Mountain
description: Ridge about 1.5 miles long forming part of the backbone ridge of St. Croix between Springgut Saddle and Lowry Hill.

name: Charlotte Amalia
description: Historic official name of the City of Saint Thomas, bestowed by King Christian V of Denmark in honor of Princess Charlotte Amalia. Often later spelled Charlotte Amalie.

name: Charlotte Amalia
description: Estate with settlement and Moravian School on the south side of Tutu Road in New Quarter, east-central St. Thomas.

name: Chenay Bay
description: Cove at the outlet of Southgate Pond west of Heiliger's Greencay Estate on the north coast of St. Croix. Old French: Anse de la Chênaie, Cove of the Oak Grove; Danish: Eglund.

name: Chocolate Hole
description: Deep cove in the southwest coast of St. John west of Buhvun Point.

name: Christian Cove
description: Inner basin of Cruz Bay north and east of Fort Christian on Battery Point.

name: Fort Christian
description: Waterfront castle battery at St. Thomas, also called Christiansfort, Kastellet, Christian’s Fort, and Fort St. Thomas or Christian.

name: Christiansted Harbor
description: Main harbor basin of Christiansted, sheltered on the north by Long Reef. Popularly called Bassin Harbor from the early French name Le Bassin.

name: Christiansted Hills
description: Irregular uplift on and east of the neck of St. Croix extending from Fredensdal to Sight Gap, divided by Springgut Notch into Jacobsberg and Carina Mountain.

name: Cinnamon Bay
description: Broad open shoal bight with a fine beach on the north shore of St. John. Name derives from Dutch Caneelboom, cinnamon tree, found on the adjacent estate.

name: Cinnamon Bay
description: Estate with bay-oil still near Cinnamon Bay, originally called Caneelboom after a cinnamon tree.

name: Cinnamon Cay
description: Small islet off Cinnamon Bay on the north shore of St. John, covered with tall grass and cactus.

name: Clairmont
description: Extensive estate in Northside B Quarter, patented to Laurence Bodkin and also known as Bodkin's Plantage. Later associated with Windsor as Mudie's Estate.

name: Clifton Hill
description: Estate named after the plateau of Clifton Hill; estate house stood on the bluff point and a fan mill below.

name: Coakley Bay
description: Curving bight on the north coast of the East End peninsula of St. Croix. Earlier French name Grand Anse.

name: Coakley Bay
description: Old estate and plantation of John Coakly Sr. with buildings on a point between two bights called Coakley Bay.

name: Cockroach Cay
description: Island north-northwest of western St. Thomas and north of Dutchcap Cay. Also called Big Cockroach, distinguishing it from Cricket Cay.

name: Cocoloba Cay
description: Steep islet east of Fish Bay, covered with sea grape growth and joined to St. John by a shallow reef.

name: Coculus Bay
description: Small bight on the south shore of St. Thomas just west of Coculus Point, sometimes confused with Bolongo Bay.

name: Coculus Point
description: Bold flat-topped bluff on the southwest side of Bolongo Bay in French Bay Quarter.

name: Coki Point
description: Low wooded hook or curving peninsula on the north side of Water Bay.

name: Coki Bay
description: Bay associated with Coki Point; also historically associated with French Baie Sand or Sand Bay.

name: Company Quarter
description: Rural district of St. Croix between Queen and Eastend Quarters and adjacent to Christiansted. Danish: Kompagniets Kvarteer.

name: Compass Point
description: Low rocky projection opposite Rotto Cay on the southern shore of Red Hook Quarter.

name: Concordia
description: Estate northeast of Riddle Point and near Concordia Bay in southeast St. John; likely identical with Saltpond Estate in later surveys.

name: Concordia
description: Estate along the north side of Centerline Road, also called Lower or South Concordia. Formerly Heiliger's Plantage.

name: Concordia
description: Moth Plantage estate in Queen Quarter, also called Upper Concordia, extending toward Concordia Bluff on the north coast.

name: Concordia Bay
description: Bay with fine sand beach east of Riddle Point on the southeast shore of St. John, near Concordia Estate and Saltpond.

name: Concordia Creek
description: Stream rising in Canaan Estate, flowing through Glynn and Concordia, and emptying into Sugar Bay as Salt River.

name: Congo Cay
description: Long narrow island north of Lovango Cay. Historic names include Cam Island, Kukelusse Kay, Lovango Chico, and Cayo Congo.

name: Constitution Hill
description: Estate on the 350-foot hill of the same name, including tracts in Queen and Company Quarters.

name: Contant
description: Estate with stone mill on a ridge northwest of Gregerie Bay. Sometimes misspelled Constant.

name: Contant
description: Estate on the brow of a hill south of Enighed Pond and north of Contant Point.

name: Contant Point
description: Salient on the northwest side of Calvary Bay entrance, south of Contant Estate.

name: Contentment
description: Small estate mainly in Contentment Valley, south of Fredensdal and Richmond Estate.

name: Contentment Gut
description: Rivulet flowing northwest through Contentment Estate.

name: Cooper Bay
description: Bight on the south coast of Prince Quarter near Cooper's Montpellier Estate; apparently identical with Negro Bay in recent survey.

name: Cooper Bay
description: Estate on the south shore of Prince Quarter, formerly owned by heirs of Alexander Cooper and also called Montpellier or Lower Negro Bay.

name: Coral Bay
description: Large deep indentation at the east end of St. John, branching into Coral Harbor, Hurricane Hole, and Round Bay.

name: Coral Bay Quarter
description: Eastern and most populous historic quarter of St. John, including Coral Bay and attached cays such as Leduck Cay and Booby Rock.

name: Coral Harbor
description: Northwest arm of Coral Bay, with anchorage for shallow-draft vessels and historic Moravian Mission base.

name: Cornhill
description: Small estate north of Manchenil Bay in Company Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Cottongarden
description: Old estate on the north coast west of East Point, with ruins near Cottongarden Bay beach. Danish equivalent: Bomuldhave.

name: Cottongarden Bay
description: Bay on the north shore of the Eastend Peninsula with sand beach and old estate ruins near shore.

name: Cottongarden Peninsula
description: Eastend B Quarter peninsula east of the isthmus between Teague Bay and Turner Hole, extending to East Point.

name: Cottongrove
description: Estate on the south coast between Mount Fancy and Robin Bay, also known as Beverhoudt's Plantage. Danish equivalent: Bomuldlund.

name: Cotton Valley
description: Plain extending back from Yellowcliff or Gulklip Bay on the north coast of Eastend B Quarter.

name: Cow Rock
description: Westernmost islet of a cluster in the southern approach to St. James Bay, sometimes paired with Calf Rock.

name: Cowell Point
description: Southern extremity of Hassel Island at the west side of St. Thomas Harbor entrance, named for Colonel Cowell.

name: Cowell Hill
description: Hill north of Cowell Point, site of an old battery and later pilot signal station.

name: Cowpet Bay
description: Shoal sheltered northwest arm of St. James Bay, east of Deck Point.

name: Crequis
description: Deep narrow forested valley about 2.5 miles long, watered by Crequis Gut and traversed by Crequis Road.

name: Crequis Gut
description: Permanent watercourse rising on the west slope of Oxford Hill, flowing through Crequis Valley and emptying on the west coast south of Sprat Hall.

name: Cricket Rock
description: Steep pinnacled islet east-northeast of Cockroach Island and north of the west end of St. Thomas.

name: Crown Bay
description: Cove on the south shore of St. Thomas northwest of Careen Hill, historically associated with cable landing and formerly called Gregerie Bay by Rohde.

name: Crown Mountain
description: Highest peak on St. Thomas, also called West Mountain or considered its summit.

name: Crown Road
description: Road continuing from Contant Road up the south slope of Crown Mountain to Crown House and down the west slope to Northside and Bonne Esperance Roads.

name: Cruz Bay
description: Village, post office, and capital of St. John, situated on the south shore of Cruz Bay at the western end of the island.

name: Cruz Bay Quarter
description: Westernmost quarter of St. John, bounded on the east by Maho Bay and Reef Bay Quarters, with attached cays including Mingo, Lovango, Congo, Henley, Ramgoat, Rata, Trunk, and Perkins.

name: Cudejarre Point
description: Sharp salient with bluff near the southeast coast of St. Croix southwest of East Point. Name adapted from French Cap de Cudejarre.

name: Current Hole
description: Passage between Water Point at the east end of St. Thomas and northwest Great St. James, divided by Current Rock.

name: Darby
description: Small plantation of Obed Darby occupying the southern half of tract 45 in Eastend A Quarter. It later became the west half of Anna’s Hope and is now part of Shoy’s Estate.

name: Darby Hill
description: Hill about half a mile east of Shoy on the southern part of tract 45, formerly Obed Darby’s plantation.

name: David Point
description: Bluff angle at the southerly extremity of Westend Quarter, forming the west entrance to Nattepan Bay and the west cove of Fortuna Bay.

name: De Beltjean Road
description: Road leaving West India Dock, crossing Sugar Estate Plain, and joining Norregade in St. Thomas City. Reserved historically for eastbound traffic.

name: Debt Hill
description: Hill on the divide and boundary between Coral Bay and Reef Bay Quarters, west-southwest of Coral Harbor and northeast of Reef Bay.

name: Deck Bay
description: Shallow bight on the east shore of southern Water Island, west-southwest of Sprat Point.

name: Deck Eyland
description: Dutch historic name for Thatch Cay northeast of St. Thomas. It appears as Deck Eyland or I. Verde, meaning Deck Island or Green Island.

name: Deck Point
description: Bluff extremity of a peninsula projecting southward on the west side of Cowpet Bay near the east end of St. Thomas.

name: De Graaff Bay
description: Historic or variant name for Druif Bay.

name: De Koks Punt
description: Dutch name for Coki Point, St. Thomas.

name: Denis Bay
description: Small reefy cove east of Perkins Cay on the northwest shore of St. John, flanked by coral reefs and offering anchorage for small craft.

name: Deripo Shoal
description: Shoal at the entrance of Christiansted Harbor, mentioned with Sandboard Shoal, Middleground, and Barracuda Shoal.

name: Detlev Point
description: Variant or map error for Ditlef Point, St. John.

name: Devers Bay
description: Small cove southeast of Chocolate Hole between Samsy and Buhvun Points on the southwest coast of St. John.

name: Diamond
description: Estate in the southwest-central portion of Prince Quarter on the south side of Centerline Road. The estate village, great house, and mill stood on a 100-foot swell east of St. George Bæk or Mint Gut and Southside Road.

name: Diamond
description: Estate 28 in Queen Quarter, a sugar plantation west of Ruby. It was called Abrahamson Plantage in 1777 before later appearing as Diamond.

name: Diamond Return
description: Estate in Company Quarter also called Little Diamond or Richardson Plantage, from John Peter Richardson. The mill stood on a hill overlooking Manchenil Bay.

name: Diamond School
description: Moravian schoolhouse on the south side of Centerline Road in the northwest corner of tract 38, Diamond Estate.

name: Diedrichs
description: Eighteenth-century estate occupying Buck Island, St. Croix, patented to town clerk John Henry Diedrichs. Ruins were reported near the summit under a large tamarind tree.

name: Diedrichs Point
description: Low projection from the south side of Buck Island, St. Croix, probably associated with the landing for old Diedrichs Estate.

name: Die Liefde
description: Dutch name for Lower Love Estate, St. Croix.

name: Din Point
description: Bold dark headland at the northeast extremity of Savann Island. The name is connected with Indo-Germanic roots for roaring or thundering noise, referring to heavy seas rushing into cliff crevices.

name: Diorite Bluff
description: Massive cliffs 20 to 40 feet high composed of diorite, along the shore between Firewood Beach and the east end of Mary Peninsula.

name: Dirk Salomons Bay
description: Old name for French Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Ditlef Trail
description: Trail from the sand beach on the east side of Rendezvous Bay northward along Ditlef Peninsula and westward to join Southside Road near Gift Hill.

name: Doerloo Bay
description: Dutch phonetic equivalent of Duurloo, the colonial family name associated with Durloe Bay and Durloe Cays.

name: Dog Island
description: Island east-southeast of Little St. James Island, known on Dutch and Danish charts as Hund or Hunde Eyland and in Spanish as Isla del Perro.

name: Dog-Island Cut
description: Boat passage between Little St. James Island and Dog Island, with a shallow rock in the middle.
aliases: El Freu de la Isla del Perro

name: Dog Point
description: Triangulation station on the east end of a rocky neck forming the eastern and highest portion of Dog Island.

name: Dog Rock
description: Highest of a group of rocks east of Dog Island, south channel of Pillsbury Sound.

name: Dolby Hill
description: Estate formerly called Montpellier, comprising tracts in Queen and Northside Quarters. Originally Peter Cornelius Low’s Plantage.

name: Domkirk Rock
description: Crag with twin steeple-shaped pinnacles resembling a cathedral, southeast of Virgin Point at the south extremity of Savann Island.

name: Donoe
description: Estate east of Wintberg Road where it turns north from Tutu Road, east of St. Thomas Harbor.

name: Donoe Hill
description: Hill immediately behind Donoe Estate, north of Tutu Road in New Quarter.

name: Dorothea
description: Estate south of Dorothea Bay on Northside Road.

name: Dorothea Bay
description: Bay on the north coast of St. Thomas between Dorothea and Hull Points, originally called Lammert Bay.

name: Dorothea Point
description: Sharp projection between Dorothea Bay and Hull Bay, formerly called Lammert Point.

name: Dorothea Road
description: Continuation of Northside Road to a col junction with Lerkelund Road and Solberg Road.

name: Dorp
description: Creole phrase di Dorp, meaning the village, used for Charlotte Amalia or St. Thomas town.

name: Dos Hermanos
description: Spanish equivalent of Two Brothers.

name: Doubloon Hill
description: Hill near the center of St. John, north-northeast of Genti Bay and west of Reef Bay Road. The name has Dutch, Danish, French, and Spanish equivalents referring to a doubloon.

name: Draabanter
description: Danish term applied to the cays adjacent to St. Thomas.

name: Drake Channel
description: Passage averaging about 3 miles wide from northeast St. John eastward along the south and southeast shores of Tortola. Entered by Sir Francis Drake in 1580.

name: Dreeket Bay
description: Indentation on the northeast shore of St. John north of the Haulover and northwest of Nancy Mill; probably the same as Haulover Bay or its southeast cove.

name: Druif Bay
description: Bay between Providence Point and Druif Point on the west shore of Water Island. Name derives from Dutch Druif, meaning grape, referring to sea grape.

name: Druif Point
description: West end of a neck separating Druif Bay from Flamingo Bay on the west shore of Water Island.

name: Dronningens Kvarter
description: Original Danish name for Queen Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Droogie
description: Sand bank or shoal north-northwest of Sandy Point, Water Island, named by Van Keulen.

name: Drunk Bay
description: Bay on the south side of Nanny Point, about 1 mile north of Ram Head on the southeast shore of St. John.

name: Dry Ledge
description: Small sandy islet or ledge off Richardsen Point west of Pull Point on the north coast of St. Croix.

name: Dry Rock
description: Rock west-southwest of Montalvan Point, Saba Cay, with nearby smaller rocks, reefs, and breakers.

name: Duchesne
description: Seventeenth-century French estate on Recovery Road where it mounts the ridge south of Christiansted.

name: Duck Cay
description: Early name for Leduck Cay, St. John.

name: Du Hamel
description: Old French estate near Anna’s Hope, St. Croix.

name: Du Monne
description: Seventeenth-century French plantation somewhere near Jolly Hill or Oxford in western St. Croix.

name: Dune Bay
description: Old name for Jack Bay, from French Anse des Dunes.

name: Dunker
description: Dunker’s Plantage at the site of Elver Estate ruins between the forks of Jealousy Gut.

name: Durloe Bay
description: Bay between Durloe Point and Kaneel Point on the northwest shore of Cruz Bay Quarter. Named for the Durloe or Duurloo family and also associated with Klein Caneel or Little Cinnamon Estate.

name: Durloe Cays
description: Three islets in the northeast entrance to Pillsbury Sound between Lovango Cay and Hognest Point: Henley, Ramgoat, and Rata Cay.

name: Dutchcap Cay
description: Dome-shaped rocky islet north-northwest of Salt Cay and off Botany Point, St. Thomas.

name: Dutchcap Passage
description: Safe passage south of Cockroach Cay near Dutchcap Cay.

name: DuVal
description: Seventeenth-century French plantation at the site of the present Canegarden Estate house on Canegarden Hill.

name: Fairplain
description: Flat on the east side of the lower course of Bethlehem Creek, there known as Fairplain Creek, extending toward the south coast of St. Croix. Once occupied by Fairplain Estate, with ruins of a residence and old mill tower south of Southside Road.

name: Fairplain Bridge
description: Southside Road bridge over Fairplain Creek, St. Croix.

name: Fairplain Creek
description: Comparatively good-sized river formed by the confluence of Jealousy Gut and Bethlehem Gut near the south coast. Its lower course is navigable by boats, but its mouth is closed by sand and mangrove thicket.

name: Fairplain
description: Old estate, tract 33b in King Quarter, later merged with Old and New Bethlehem by De Forrest.

name: Falaise
description: French descriptive name applied to Canegarden Bluff on the south coast of St. Croix.

name: Fanny’s Fancy
description: Estate at the west point of Rod Bay, Eastend B Quarter, St. Croix, comprising parts of Bourn Plantage and Richardsen holdings.

name: Fareham
description: Estate in Eastend A Quarter on the south coast of St. Croix, including Fareham or Nugent Hill, estatehouse and mill near Fareham Bay, and land later transferred from Prospect Hill. Fareham Bay was known in old French as Anse du Milord.

name: Fareham Hill
description: Prominent point on the west side of Great Pond Bay, east of Fareham Mill and east of Nugent Estate, now part of Fareham Estate.

name: Fareham Point
description: Rocky turn at the east side of Fareham Bay on the south coast of St. Croix. The whole abutment of Fareham or Nugent Hill was also associated with Cap du Milord or Milord Point.

name: Farrington
description: Estate in Eastend A Quarter, property of Eliza Farrington in 1754. Hartman Mill is now at the southeast corner.

name: Perkins Kay
description: Oxholm spelling of Perkins Cay, St. John.

name: Ferrall Point
description: Bend of the south coast of St. Croix on the east side of Halfpenny Bay, on Dr. Ferrall’s old woodland tract.

name: Verskrand
description: Danish equivalent of Verswater Pan.

name: Vessup Bay
description: Inner portion of Redhook Bay, historically also identified on some charts as Vessup Bight. Dutch Binnewater means enclosed water, fitting the inlet form.

name: Firewood Beach
description: Bight of gravel and sand fringed with coral reef on the Narrows, north coast of St. John.

name: Fish Bay
description: Shallow sandy and weedy inlet between Cocoloba Cay and Ditlef Point, with anchorage at the entrance.

name: Fishbay
description: Estate at the head of Fish Bay in Reef Bay Quarter, St. John.

name: Fish Cay
description: Small islet with adjacent boulders in St. James Bay, west of Great St. James Island.

name: Fish Cay
description: Name sometimes applied to Cocoloba Cay.

name: Fish Point
description: Northwest extremity of Inner Brass Island, named for good fishing in the vicinity.

name: Fjord Saltriver
description: Danish form referring to Salt River Bay, St. Croix.

name: Flag Hill
description: Point on the line between New Quarter and French Bay Quarter. Early maps note that a Danish flag was displayed there when ships arrived and that watch was kept on the hill.

name: Flaggenberg
description: Old estate on Flag Hill, St. Thomas.

name: Flagstok Hill
description: Hill north-northwest of Hope Estate on the ridge between Stumpy Bay and Santa Maria Bay. The Danish name means flagstaff.

name: Flamingo Bay
description: Bay on the southwest shore of Water Island, also called Flamingopan Bay from the pond immediately east.

name: Flamingo Hill
description: Hill between Flamingo Bay and Flamingo Point at the south end of Water Island.

name: Flamingopan Bay
description: Northwest cove of Perseverance Bay. The name more properly applies to the saltmarsh between Perseverance Estate and the coral-sand beach.

name: Flamingo Point
description: Brown rocky cliff about 100 feet high at the south end of Water Island.

name: Flamingo Pond
description: Mangrove-bordered pond east of Flamingo Bay beach, Water Island.

name: Flamingo Pond
description: Saltmarsh near Perseverance Estate, separated by a coral-sand beach from Perseverance Bay. Heavy rains convert it into a pond.

name: Flamingo Rock
description: Rock joined by a low rocky neck to Flamingo Point, Water Island.

name: Flanagan Island
description: Island southeast of Privateer Point, St. John, with adjacent rocks and ledges bringing total area to about 22.16 acres.

name: Flanagan Passage
description: Channel system between St. John and Norman Island, including passages around Flanagan Island and Indian Rocks.

name: Flat Cay
description: Larger of the Flat Cays southwest of Red Point, St. Thomas.

name: Flat Cays
description: Two islets southwest of Red Point and northeast of Saba Cay. The larger is Big Flat or Raso; the smaller is Rasito or Little Flat.

name: Flemingham Cay
description: Variant name for Flanagan Island.

name: Flemish Cap
description: Alternative name for Dutchcap Cay.

name: Fogarthy Castle
description: Name by which Bluebeard Castle was known after Thim Fogarthy bought and lived in it beginning in 1800. It later passed through several owners and names.

name: Fondeadero de la Isla del Agua
description: Spanish name for Water Island Anchorage.

name: Footer Point
description: Turn of shoreline between Water Bay and Smith Bay on the northeast coast of St. Thomas, with a hill behind it.

name: Foretop
description: Sailors’ name for French Hill, St. Thomas.

name: Fortberg
description: Conspicuous hill on the small peninsula separating Coral Harbor from Hurricane Hole, named from the ruins of an old fort. In 1733 the garrison was surprised and massacred during the slave revolt.

name: Fort Catharina
description: Abandoned battery on a hill beside the west shore road north of Frederiksted, on the boundary between Northside A and Westend Quarters.

name: Fort Christian
description: Government station and battery at Cruz Bay, St. John, called Christiansfort by the Danes.

name: Fort Christiansværn
description: Fort at Christiansted, St. Croix. Danish værn means defense.

name: Fort Louise Augusta
description: Battery on a projecting rock point at the east side of Christiansted Harbor. The French had a battery here in 1671 named Fort Saint Jean. Also called Pyntbatteriet by the Danes.

name: Fort Sofia Frederika
description: Early battery at the north end of Protestant Cay, built to defend Christiansted. Now in ruins.

name: Fortuna
description: Old estate in St. Thomas with ruins of estatehouse and mill on Fortuna Hill.

name: Fortuna Bay
description: Bay on the south coast of St. Thomas between David and Lucas Points, consisting of Nattepan Bay to the west and Backefall or Krabbepan Bay to the east.

name: Fortuna Cliff
description: Cliff along the south shore east of Lucas Point and along the shores of Fortuna Bay.

name: Fortuna Hill
description: Highest summit on Westend Peninsula, about a mile from the south shore and east of Westend Point.

name: Fortuna Mill
description: Ruined sugar mill near the ruins of old Fortuna Estatehouse, southwest of Fortuna Hill.

name: Fountain
description: Estate of Major de Nully occupying the upper valley with the headstreams of Jealousy Bæk. Also called Big Fountain.

name: Fountain
description: Same as Little Fountain Estate, tract 3 in King Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Fox
description: Estate in Prince Quarter about one mile from the south coast, associated with tracts formerly owned by Cunningham’s heirs and Thomas Lake Sr.

name: Française
description: Reference to French Bay, St. Thomas.

name: France Gereformeerde Kerk
description: Dutch chart label for a French Reformed Church probably located at French Hill, associated with Huguenot settlement.

name: Francis Bay
description: Bay enclosed on the north by Whistling Cay and Mary Point, with fine sand beach and protected anchorage.

name: Francois Bay
description: Alternative name for Sugar Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Frank Bay
description: Open cove just south of Cruz Bay and north of Moravian Point.

name: Franske Seiler
description: Danish name for Sail Rock in Virgin Passage.

name: Franskmandeklipper
description: Old Danish name of Sail Rock.

name: Fransmanns oder Vogel-Klippe
description: German form for Frenchman Cap, also described as a bird rock where gulls and other birds nested.

name: Fransmanuar
description: Alternative name of Caravella or Sail Rock, probably a corruption of French Man-of-War.

name: Frauen Kay
description: Oxholm name for Henley Cay, the largest of the Durloe Cays.

name: Fredensborg
description: Estate near a 430-foot hill southeast of the fork of Water Bay Road and Mandal Road, between Anna’s Retreat and Frydendal.

name: Fredensberg
description: Moravian mission station in Frederiksted, St. Croix. The name means Peace Mountain.

name: Fredensborg
description: Estate in central King Quarter, Danish name meaning Citadel of Peace. It was the plantation of Captain Martin Heytiger or Heiliger.

name: Fredensborg Hill
description: Northernmost knoll of Kingshill Ridge, St. Croix.

name: Fredensdal
description: Moravian mission station with churches, well, and cemetery in Company Quarter. Danish form of German Friedensthal, meaning Valley of Peace.

name: Fredensfeld
description: Important Moravian mission station in the southeast corner of tract 9, Mon Bijou Estate. German Friedensfeld and Danish Fredensfelt mean Field of Peace.

name: Frederik Battery
description: Old fort on Frederik Point, Hassel Island.

name: Frederik Point
description: Easternmost angle of Hassel Island, marked by an old fort on the west side of St. Thomas Harbor entrance. Originally called Jansen Point or West Hook.

name: Frederik Knoll
description: Rocky patch on the west side of St. Thomas Harbor entrance off Frederik Point.

name: Frederiksberg
description: Hill rising from the north shore of St. Thomas Harbor and surmounted by Bluebeard Tower or Bluebeard Castle.

name: Frederiksberg Point
description: Bluff shore angle at the foot of Frederiksberg on the north side of Long Bay, St. Thomas Harbor.

name: Frederiksfort
description: Fort on the west coast at the mouth of a stream northwest of Frederiksted. Also called Fort Frederik.

name: Frederiksfort
description: Thirty-four-foot tower built on Frederiksberg or Bluebeard Hill by the Danish Government in 1689, now called Bluebeard Castle.

name: Frederikshaab
description: Estate east of Frederiksted, later united with Wheel of Fortune. Danish name meaning Frederik’s Hope.

name: Frederiksted Road
description: Anchorage ground in Westend Bay adjacent to Frederiksted, also called Frederiksted Harbor.

name: Fredrikdal
description: Valley opening on Leinster Bay with a lagoon or pond behind the beach, traversed by Northside Road.

name: Freeze Bay
description: Semicircular indentation midway between Lagoon Point and Sabbat Point on the west side of Coral Bay.

name: French Bay
description: Bay on the south coast of St. Thomas, east-southeast of Muhlenfels Point.

name: Frenchbay
description: Estate, plantation, or stock farm on the hillside northwest of the beach at French Bay.

name: French Bay Quarter
description: Quarter of St. Thomas embracing the south shore from Patrick Point west to St. Thomas Harbor, bounded by Redhook and New Quarters. Capella Cays are attached to this quarter.

name: French Bay Road
description: Road leaving East Road southeast of Havensight Point and extending southwest to French Bay.

name: Frenchcap Cay
description: Steep rocky grass-covered islet southeast of the Capella Islands and south of St. Thomas. Known by several names in Danish, French, Spanish, and English.

name: French Hill
description: Westernmost of three rounded spurs behind St. Thomas city, named for French Huguenots who took refuge and settled nearby.

name: Fren de Santiago
description: Spanish name of St. James Cut.

name: Fries Point
description: Point on the west shore of Coral Bay between Freeze Bay and Lagoon Point.

name: Frises Bay
description: Name assigned by Oxholm to present Johns Folly Bay or possibly another indentation near Sabbat Point; modern surveys place Freeze Bay farther north.

name: Frydendal
description: Estate near the north coast of St. Thomas and east of Water Bay. Danish name meaning Vale of Delight.

name: Fugleklippen
description: Danish name for Frenchman Cap or Frenchcap Cay.

name: Fungi Passage
description: Strait or cut between Whistling Cay and Mary Point on the northern coast of St. John.

name: Furnel
description: Old estate at a sharp rocky salient on the east side of Stewart or Wills Bay. The associated ridge is now part of Mount Stewart Estate.

name: Gabriel Point
description: Alternative name or misreading of Cabrita Point, St. Thomas.

name: Galeota
description: Spanish equivalent of French La Galiote, one of the historic names of Sail Rock.

name: Galge Bay
description: Outer cove on the south side of Cruz Bay between Galge Point and Battery Point. The Danish name means gallows; locally also called Gallows Bay.

name: Galge Bay
description: Danish name of Gallows Bay, St. Croix.

name: Galge Point
description: North angle of a small neck on the south side of Cruz Bay entrance. Danish name means gallows.

name: La Galiote
description: Early French name for Sail Rock, also called La Caravelle and Le Heu.

name: Gallows Bay
description: English equivalent of Galge Bay on St. John.

name: Gallows Bay
description: Cowl-shaped cove in Christiansted Harbor on the east side of Christiansted, west of Mount Welcome.

name: Gallows Hill
description: Same as Honduras Hill or Chacha Hill in Southside Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Ganee Hill
description: Creole corruption of Kaneel Hill, St. John.

name: Garden of Wismenog
description: Non-existent chart label caused by misreading two adjacent legends on Oxholm’s map: Carden’s Estate and Battery of Wismenog.

name: Gasling
description: Plantages of George Gasling, including Ruan Bay Estate in Westend Quarter and Mint in Prince Quarter.

name: Gaudri
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage on a hill south of Altona, St. Croix.

name: Gedebukken
description: Danish equivalent of Buck Island, St. Croix.

name: Genti Bay
description: North or landward portion of Reef Bay, separated from the rest of Reef Bay by coral reefs and a motor-boat channel.

name: George Hill
description: Hill east-northeast of Frederiksted on tract 26, Robe Hill Estate. Also called St. George Hill or Signal Hill.

name: George Hill
description: Variant estate name of St. George Hill or Robe Hill Estate, Armstrong Plantage.

name: Georges Bæk
description: Stream flowing past Cassava Garden, St. Croix; noted as a duplicate name five miles west.

name: Gerd de Wint
description: Two plantages designated on Oldendorp’s 1767 map of St. Thomas: one southeast of Wintberg and north-northwest of Tutu; the other north of Girgirri Bay.

name: Gerigeri
description: Name applied to bodies of water from an indigenous tree known by variants such as Bigiri, Girgirri, Gregerie, Gregory, Grigri, Grugru, Kriki, and Crequis. The tree was also called French Oak.

name: Gibbs
description: Plantage tract 12 in King Quarter, St. Croix, patrimony of William Gibbs’ heirs.

name: Gift Hill
description: Summit north of Rendezvous Bay, on the mountain mass between Bans Gut and Fish Bay and on the boundary between Cruz Bay and Reef Bay Quarters. Locally known as Sessman Hill.

name: Gift Hill Road
description: Trail from Centerline Road south along the ridge to Sessman Estate at Gift Hill, meeting Jinny Gut Road and continuing to Monte.

name: Gigiri
description: Variant spelling of Gerigeri or Gregerie, an oaklike tree name also used in bay names.

name: Girard
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage about the northwest corner of Southgate Pond, St. Croix.

name: Girgirri Bay
description: Indentation of the southern shore of St. Thomas opposite Water Island, historically spelled Girgirri, Grigri, and Gregerie. See Gregerie Bay.

name: Glynn
description: Estate in Concordia Valley south of Baron Bluff, comprising tracts in King and Queen Quarters. Also called The Glynn and erroneously The Gynn.

name: Goat Hill
description: Same as Sugarloaf Hill, St. Croix.

name: Goat Hills
description: Broken ridge running west from East Point, St. Croix, with two chief peaks: Sugarloaf Hill and Hughes Hill.

name: Goat Island
description: Alternative name for Buck Island, St. Croix.

name: Goat Rock
description: Outstanding boulder near the southwest shore of Little Hans Lollik Island.

name: Gobé
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage between Longford and Manchenil Bay, St. Croix.

name: Godthank
description: Estate on a ridge southeast of Bordeaux Hill, Westend Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Golden Grove
description: Estate in Prince Quarter, St. Croix, called Irwins Plantage after John Irvin, proprietor in 1754.

name: Golden Rock
description: Estate on the west shore of Christiansted Harbor, west of Protestant Cay. Also spelled Goldenrock and later united with Little Princess as Phillips’ Estate.

name: Goldring Rock
description: Local name of Packet Rock.

name: Goodchild
description: Reference to Clermont Estate, St. Croix.

name: Goodhope
description: Estate in Westend Quarter on the south coast of St. Croix, originally John Smitt’s Plantage.

name: Good Hope
description: English translation of Bonne Esperance Estate in Queen Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Gorret Rock
description: Small dry rock off the southwest point of Dutchcap Cay. Spanish gorrete means small cap.

name: Gorro Flamenco
description: Spanish name of Dutchcap or Dutchman’s Cap.

name: Gosling Bay
description: Bay on the north coast of St. Croix noted by Eggers as habitat of Cnaemalium. George Gasling was original proprietor of Ruan Bay on the south coast.

name: Government Hill
description: Easternmost of three hills behind St. Thomas City, surmounted by a stone tower long called Kjær’s Tower and locally Blackbeard’s Castle.

name: Government Station
description: Government station on Battery Point at Cruz Bay, St. John.

name: Governor Hill
description: Hill on tract 50 in Queen Quarter, residence of M. du Bois, French governor of the island in the seventeenth century; later called Governor’s Castle.

name: Gravel Bay
description: Small bight with gravel beach in the northwest part of Haulover Bay, north shore of Eastend Peninsula, St. John.

name: Gras-Kaien
description: Alternative of Bokken Eiland or Buck Island, described as a small island between Frenchcap and St. Thomas.

name: Gras Pynt
description: Danish name of Grass Point on the south coast of St. Croix.

name: Grambokola Hill
description: Summit of the peninsular headland between Mosquito Bay and Krum Bay.

name: Grambokola
description: Prominent wooded peninsula projecting south between Mosquito Bay and Krum Bay.

name: Granard
description: Estate in southern Company Quarter, enveloping Cornhill and most of Diamond Return except on the south.

name: Grande Anse
description: French historic name for Coakley Bay on the north coast of St. Croix.

name: Grande Baye de Bordeaux
description: French name for Bordeaux Bay, used to distinguish it from Little Bordeaux Bay.

name: Granderie
description: Old French estate in Crequis Valley near a hill overlooking William, St. Croix.

name: Grande Cannebay
description: French name for Great Cane Bay, shown east of present Cane Bay at Lavallee where later charts place Little Cane Bay.

name: Grand Fond
description: French name meaning great bottom or commodious anchorage, applied to Limetree Bay on the south coast of Queen Quarter.

name: Grand Princess
description: English equivalent of La Grande Princesse Estate, St. Croix.

name: Grand S. James
description: French name for Great St. James Island.

name: Grange
description: Estate 9 in Company Quarter, St. Croix, Roger Ferrall Plantage.

name: Grange
description: Old French plantage near Glynn, St. Croix.

name: Grange Gut
description: Stream about four miles long, rising in Hermon Hill and flowing through Grange, Anna’s Hope, Peter’s Rest, Pearl, Cassava Garden, and Jerusalem Estates to Limetree Bay.

name: Grange Stockfarm
description: North half of tract 22, Joseph Richardsen plantage, Company Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Grange Valley
description: Valley between Grange and Anna’s Hope on the north and Work-and-Rest Hills on the south.

name: Grapetree Bay
description: Open bight on the south coast of St. Croix between Hughes Point and Grapetree Point, with bluff shore, coral reef barrier, and beach opening at the west end.

name: Grasklip Point
description: Detached islet at the southeast end of Outer Brass Island, same as Grass Point or Gras Point.

name: Grass Bay
description: Historic name for Rod Bay or the eastern half of Carty Point on the south coast of Eastend Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Grass Cay
description: Long narrow cay attached to Eastend Quarter, St. Thomas, west of Mingo Cay and separated from Thatch Cay by Middle Passage.

name: Grass Point
description: Long narrow salient projecting from the south coast of St. Croix at Madame Carty’s old estate, between Rod Bay and Turner Hole.

name: Great Bay
description: Bay indenting the eastern end of St. Thomas between Cabrita Point and Water Point. Formerly called Current Hole, now restricted to the passage nearby.

name: Great Centerline
description: Base line of the St. Croix land survey begun in 1734 by Governor Frederik Moth, used to lay out plantation tracts.

name: Great Cruz Bay
description: Former common English chart name for what is now officially Calvary Bay.

name: Great Gut
description: Small stream descending from a ravine on the western slope of Mount Washington and emptying into the sea between Butler Bay and Sprat Hole.

name: Great Krum Bay
description: Alternative name for Krum Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Great Lameshur Bay
description: Easternmost and largest arm of Lameshur Bay, affording good shelter under the lee of Cabrithorn Point.

name: Great Middleground
description: Outlying shoal east of Long Reef and north-northwest of Fort Louise Augusta, St. Croix.

name: Great Northside
description: Quarter of St. Thomas embracing the northern shore and slope from Dorothea Point to Tutu Bay, part of the northern environs of St. Thomas City, and the Hans Lollik Islands.

name: Great Northside Bay
description: Historic name for Magens Bay, also called Buck, Northside, or Store-Nordside Bay.

name: Great Pond
description: Broad shallow lagoon sometimes dry, separated from Great Pond Bay by a narrow barrier. Also called Great Saltpond.

name: Greatpond
description: Estate in Eastend A Quarter on the south coast of St. Croix, named from adjacent Great Pond.

name: Great Pond Bay
description: Sandy bight on the south coast of St. Croix west of East Point, named from adjacent Great Pond.

name: Great Princess
description: Translation of La Grande Princesse Estate, to distinguish it from Little Princess Estate.

name: Green Cay
description: Brushy islet southeast of French Bay, St. Thomas, with nearby dry or awash rocks.

name: Green Cay
description: Islet off the north coast of St. Croix west of Pull Point and east-northeast of Fort Louise Augusta. French maps called it Ile Verte, sometimes confused with Buck Island.

name: Greencay
description: Estate on the north coast between Chenay Bay and Prune Bay, including tract 14 patented to Pieter Heyliger with later accretions.

name: Green Cay Point
description: Name used in station descriptions for Punnett Point.

name: Gregerie
description: Beach on the south coast of St. Thomas from near Nisky to the point where Mosquito Bay Road reaches the shore.

name: Gregerie Bank
description: Shoal composed of dead coral and sand in Gregerie Bay or West Gregerie Channel, northwest of Sand Point and from Banana Point, Water Island.

name: Gregerie Bay
description: Indentation from Crown Bay to Little Krum Bay on the south shore of St. Thomas opposite Water Island. Originally synonymous with Crown Bay and later extended to nearby channels and harbor waters.

name: Gregerie Channel
description: Passage between Water Island and St. Thomas, including East Gregerie Channel, Gregerie Harbor, and West Gregerie Channel.

name: Gregerie Harbor
description: Well-sheltered basin or small sound embracing Gregerie Bay and extending across to Water Island between Banana Point and Caroline Point.

name: Gregeriet
description: Danish equivalent of Dutch De Grigri, originally referring to a conspicuous grigri tree on Crown Bay shore and later extended to the bay and beach west toward Nisky.

name: Gregory
description: Variant spelling of Gerigeri, Gigiri, Grigri, and Grugru, a tree name used in place names.

name: Greig Hill
description: Hill west of Salt River Bay near the sharp point at Sugar Bay entrance, site of old Greig’s Fort.

name: Greig’s Fort
description: Battery near the west side of Sugar Bay entrance on Greig Hill.

name: Grigri Bay
description: Original authentic form of the name later known as Gregerie Bay. Van Keulen’s chart shows a Grigri tree near the shore of the bay.

name: Groen Eyland
description: Dutch name of Green Cay, St. Thomas.

name: Grøn Kay
description: Danish name of Greencay Estate or Green Cay, St. Croix.

name: Grønkeybayen
description: Danish name meaning Green Cay Bay, probably the same as Chenay Bay.

name: Groot Bay
description: Dutch name meaning Great or Large Bay, applied by Oxholm to Johnson Bay and Crocapan Bay.

name: Groote Lameshuur Bay
description: Dutch form of Great Lameshur Bay.

name: Groote Noordsyde Bay
description: Dutch name for Magens Bay or Great Northside Bay.

name: Grootpan Bay
description: Bay along the east shore of Cabrithorn Peninsula in southeast St. John. Dutch name means Great Pond, from the large saltpond northeast of it.

name: Gross Cruxbay
description: Old German-Latin-English hybrid name for Calvary Bay, meaning Great Cross Bay.

name: Grosse Nordseite Bay
description: German name for Magens Bay or Great Northside Bay.

name: Grosse Pointe du Nord
description: French name meaning Great North Point, used by Bellin for Picara Point, formerly also called Great Northside Point.

name: Gross Hans Lollik
description: German form of Hans Lollik Island.

name: Gross Krumbay
description: German name for Krum Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Gross S. James
description: German name of Great St. James Island.

name: Ground Rock
description: Detached bare rock near the east point of Hans Lollik Island.

name: Grouper Point
description: Eastern extremity of Thatch Cay.

name: Grove
description: Estate in Eastend B Quarter, St. Croix, on the east half of tract 11. Ruins, chimney, and row of pillars were found at Cotton Valley Trail’s end.

name: Groveplace
description: Estate in central Prince Quarter, part of John Baker’s Plantage and later Plasket’s Estate including Hardlabor.

name: Guardhouse Point
description: English translation of the Danish name Vagthus Point. The dictionary notes Watchhouse Point or Watch Ho would be better translations.

name: Guava Valley
description: Jochumsdal east of Adrian, St. John, where guavas grow wild in several groves.

name: Guillarmet
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage or estate on a hill southeast of a point on the south shore of Altona Lagoon, St. Croix.

name: Gut
description: Local term for creek beds, whether perennial or intermittent, and also for an entire drainage basin or valley floor.

name: Hacienda del Retiro de Ana
description: Spanish name of Anna’s Retreat or Tutu Estate, St. Thomas.

name: Hafen
description: German term used by Moravian missionaries for the harbor of St. Thomas.

name: Halfpenny Bay
description: Open curving bight on the south coast of St. Croix, south of Longford and opposite Christiansted. Old French name Anse à Galet.

name: Ham Bay
description: Open shoal bay west-southwest of Ham Bluff on the northwest coast of St. Croix. Locally called Ham’s Bay.

name: Hamby
description: Estate deeded to John Farrington, with village at the mouth of Caledonia Valley on the east side of Ham Bay. Locally called Hamsbay.

name: Ham Bluff
description: Remarkable headland on the northwest coast of St. Croix, called Cap du Diable by early French navigators and Morro Hams or Cabo del Diablo in Spanish. The bluff rises steeply toward Maroon Ridge and Ham Peak.

name: Ham Bluff Lighthouse
description: White cylindrical tower on Ham Bluff, visible 27 miles and historically listed as a group-flashing white light station.

name: Hambluff Valley
description: Basin of Roger Gut, also called Hambluff Bæk, debouching on the northwest coast immediately west of Ham Bluff.

name: Hammer Farm
description: Estate east of Adrian and south of Peter Peak, connected to Cinnamon Bay by a tortuous mountain road. It is at or near old Catherineberg.

name: Hammer-Farm Road
description: Road leaving Northside Road at Cinnamon Bay, zigzagging up the slope and then ascending south to the ridge before turning west to Hammer Farm and joining Centerline Road.

name: Hannah’s Rest
description: Estate south of Centerline Road and near the south coast of St. Croix, originally belonging to William Heylinger and later squatters’ land producing cane, grass, and truck crops.

name: Hanseatic Rock
description: Variant name for Hans Lollik Rock.

name: Hansen Bay
description: Northeast cove of Round Bay, St. John. Some authorities made Hansen Bay coextensive with Round Bay.

name: Hansen Bay
description: Original name of Hull Bay on the north shore of St. Thomas, appearing as Jurriaan Hansen Bay and Hansens-Bay.

name: Hans-Lollik Island
description: Island northeast of Picara Peninsula off the north shore of St. Thomas. Lollik refers to a native of Laaland, Denmark, so the name may mean Hans the Laalander or refer to a forgotten mariner or colonist.

name: Hans-Lollik Islands
description: Group lying off the middle of the north shore of St. Thomas, consisting of Hans-Lollik Island, Little Hans-Lollik, Pelican Cay, and Hans-Lollik Rock.

name: Hans Lollik Rock
description: Rock awash and always breaking southeast of the south end of Hans-Lollik Island.

name: Hans Sorensen’s Ground
description: Same as Sorensen Ground in Christiansted Harbor.

name: Harung
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage near Merle Run, near a hill west of Cottage or about Sion Farm.

name: Harbor Point
description: Southern extremity of the peninsula between Coral Harbor and Hurricane Hole.

name: Harden Gut
description: Gut rising in Concordia Estate, flowing northwest through Wheel-of-Fortune and Lagrange, and emptying into Grange Gut at the northeast corner of Frederiksted.

name: Hardlabor
description: Estate tract 5 of Prince Quarter, patrimony of Alexander Cooper’s heirs. It also included tract 13 north of Groveplace and was later attached to Groveplace as Plasket’s Estate.

name: Hart Bay
description: Western cove of Rendezvous Bay, St. John.

name: Hartman
description: Estate bordering the west shores of Great Pond and Great Pond Bay in Eastend A Quarter. Hartman’s Plantage first appears on Oldendorp’s 1767 map.

name: Hartmann
description: Name applied to Limetree Estate, St. Croix.

name: Hassel Island
description: Island forming the western side of St. Thomas Harbor, also historically known as Orkanshullet Island.

name: Haulover
description: Narrowest part of Eastend Peninsula between Dreeket or Haulover Bay on the northeast coast and the opposite cove of Round Bay. Oxholm named it Overhale.

name: Haulover Bay
description: Bay on the north shore of Eastend Peninsula between Graved Point and Dreeket Point; the only practicable anchorage in that region.

name: Havensight
description: Estate on a hill on the east side of St. Thomas Harbor commanding a wide harbor view. Danish Havnsigte means harbor view.

name: Havensight Point
description: Point on the east shore of St. Thomas Harbor northwest of Havensight Estatehouse, marked by Havensight wood jetty.

name: Hawk Hill
description: Flat-topped summit southwest of Crown Mountain on the boundary between Westend Quarter and Southside Quarter, northeast of Brewers Bay.

name: Haypiece Hill
description: Hill east of Krum Bay on the southern coast of St. Thomas.

name: Hedou
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage on the shore of Limetree Bay east of the mouth of Grange Gut.

name: Heerlin
description: Two old plantages in St. Thomas: one south of the east end of Magens Bay and east-northeast of Lerkelund, and another between Longford and Jersey Bay.

name: Heilyger
description: Oldendorp’s spelling for plantages otherwise spelled Heytiger or Heyliger by Beck.

name: Heitman
description: Plantage of Frederik Christian Heitman, associated with Frederikshaab, St. Croix.

name: Helm
description: Herman Helm’s widow held title in 1754 to the estate later known as Beckman’s and now Sally’s Fancy.

name: Hemers
description: Plantage also called Hemers Plantage, the same as Judith’s Fancy Estate.

name: Hendrichsen
description: Proprietor of a tract in the elbow of Westend Saltpond, now part of Camporico.

name: Hendrik Bay
description: Cove with beach and coconut grove on the east side of Santa Maria Bay, south of Vluck Point on the north shore of St. Thomas.

name: Henley Cay
description: Largest of the three Durloe Cays off the northwestern coast of St. John.

name: Hensler
description: Oldendorp indicates several estates among the Westend Hills near Bordeaux Hill but names only Henslers Plantagen.

name: Herb Bay
description: Bight near Hope, northwest of Long Point on the south shore of Westend Quarter, from French Anse aux Herbes.

name: Hermitage
description: Estate house and stockfarm at the north end of Borck Creek, Eastend Quarter, St. John. Erroneously located on the Haulover by some.

name: Hermitage
description: Estate in an enclosed valley near the sources of Bethlehem Gut, including tracts in Prince and King Quarters formerly owned by John Willett and his heirs.

name: Hermon Hill
description: Hill southwest of Christiansted, St. Croix.

name: Hermon Hill
description: Estate almost coextensive with old Lillie Plantage in Company Quarter, extending east to Signal Hill. Estatehouse was on Hermon Hill southwest of Christiansted.

name: Hesselberg
description: Estate at the northeast end of Westend Saltpond. Engelb. Hesselberg owned the original tract in 1754. Later united with Wheel-of-Fortune along with Smithfield and Stonyground.

name: Het Dorp Scharlotte Amelia
description: Dutch name meaning The Village Charlotte Amelia. It was replaced in common use by Het Dorp, Di Dorp, Byen, Tappus, and officially by Amalienborg or Saint Thomas.

name: Le Heu
description: French name meaning the Hoy, one of the names applied by Bellin to Sail Rock, along with Caravelle and Galiote.

name: Hoehste Berg
description: German designation referring to Mount Eagle, St. Croix.

name: Hodge
description: Estate fronting a bay between Kopman Point and Pow Point on the north coast of Eastend B Quarter.

name: Hoe Hill
description: Hill southwest of Molendal and northwest of Genti Bay, St. John.

name: Hoffman
description: Estate south of Tutu Road at Charlotte Amalia Estate, St. Thomas.

name: Hogensborg
description: Estate on the north side of Centerline Road with village east of Frederiksted. Properly Høgensborg, a Danish name meaning City of the Hawk; also known by alternative Sorgenfrie.

name: Høgensborg Gut
description: Perennial brook rising near Robe Hill, flowing through Carlton and past Høgensborg Estate village to the south coast northwest of Long Point.

name: Hognest Bay
description: Bay indenting the northwest shore of St. John on the east side of Hognest Peninsula. The name probably derives from adjacent Hognest Point.

name: Hognest Hill
description: Hill southwest of Hognest Point at the north end of Hognest Peninsula.

name: Hognest Peninsula
description: Peninsula terminating in Hognest Hill and Hognest Point on the west side of Hognest Bay.

name: Hognest Point
description: Northern end of rocky Hognest Peninsula projecting from the northwest shore of St. John. The dictionary rejects Hawknest, Hogness, and Hogsnest as preferred forms.

name: Hognest Rock
description: Rock close inshore just north of Hognest Point.

name: Højlandet
description: Danish name applied to the mountain mass in the northwest portion of St. Croix west of Jealousy Gut.

name: Høiland
description: Danish name applied to a hill east of Bovoni Bay and south of Bovoni Estate.

name: Holenberg
description: Old plantage or estate west of Jersey Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Holm Rock Island
description: Danish-English hybrid reference to Buck Island off St. Croix; Oxholm Cay was proposed.

name: Honduras Hill
description: Knoll on the isthmus north of Careen Hill separating St. Thomas Harbor from Crown Bay. Also called Gallows Hill.

name: Hontufa
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage near Princess Estate village, St. Croix.

name: Hope
description: Estate on Westend Road between Stumpy Bay and Santa Maria Bay. A trail runs southwest to the old sugar mill at Fortuna; a nearby cove may be called Hope Bay.

name: Hope
description: Estate northeast of Reef Bay and southwest of Debt Hill, east of the road running north.

name: Hope
description: Estate on the south coast of Westend Quarter, originally John Jelliff’s Plantage. It included tract 12 except a northern strip, and tract 3 south of Centerline Road.

name: Hope
description: Estate in southwest Queen Quarter north of the east end of Krause Lagoon, chiefly sugar cane with grassland and mangrove next to shore.

name: Hope
description: Estate 23 in Prince Quarter, bisected by Mint Gut and walled by steep ridges. It was the plantage of William Schafer or Schoffer.

name: Hope Gut
description: Stream about one mile long reaching the shore just west of Hope Mill on the south coast of Westend Quarter.

name: Horn’s Bay
description: Old name of Botany Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Horse Hill
description: Flat grassy peak of a ridge forming the western spur of Maroon Ridge and the north wall of Caledonia Valley or Springgarden Gut near the northwest corner of St. Croix.

name: Hospital
description: Hospital grounds adjoining Christiansted on the southeast, with buildings on a spur of Recovery Ridge.

name: Hospital
description: Hospital north of St. Thomas Harbor on the hills of St. Thomas.

name: Hovell
description: Plantage associated with Springs Estate in Eastend A Quarter. The proprietor name on Beck may read Abraham Hovell, Senior.

name: Hovedkjøden
description: Danish name applied to the main mountain ridge of St. Thomas; also called Bjærgryggen.

name: Hou
description: One of the historic names for Sail Rock, also called Bergantin, Carvel, Heu, Hoy, and Hoya.

name: Høyeste Bjerg
description: Danish legend on Oxholm’s map of St. John between Camelberg Peak and the nearby northern summit.

name: Hoyo de la Corriente
description: Spanish equivalent of Current Hole, associated with Water Point, Great Bay, and the Current Hole passage.

name: Hoyo del Huracán
description: Spanish name for Hurricane Hole, St. John.

name: Hughes
description: Old estate on the south coast of Eastend Peninsula, with a projecting rounded bluff between Grapetree Bay and Jack Bay.

name: Hughes Plantage
description: Old name of Nugent Estate in Eastend A Quarter, property of Betsalie Hughes.

name: Hull
description: Estate on the shore of Hull Bay, identified with Ensomhed.

name: Hull Bay
description: Bay between Tropaco Point and Dorothea Point, separated from Magens Bay by Tropaco Peninsula. Formerly known as Jurriaan Hansen Bay, Hansen Bay, Ensomhed Bay, Little Northside Bay, and locally Hull Bay.

name: Hull Point
description: Local name for Tropaco Point, St. Thomas.

name: Humbug
description: Estate in Queen Quarter, St. Croix, plantage of Nicolas Salomon. Misspelled Hambug and Humbng in some sources.

name: Hunde Eyland
description: Original Dutch or Danish name of Dog Island.

name: Hurricane Hole
