description: Middle and northernmost of three main arms of Coral Bay, providing the safest hurricane anchorage except from the southeast. It contains coves including Battery Beach, Jewfish Cove, Popilleau Bay, Borck Creek, Princess Bay, Otter Creek, Water Creek, Careen Cove, and Nathaniel Bay.

name: Hvide Sand Bay
description: Danish name for Whitesand Bay, St. John.

name: Nadir
description: Estate on the slopes of Nadir Ridge, about 400 to 600 yards north or east of Mangrove Lagoon in Redhook Quarter, St. Thomas. Map 3240 and Zabriskie locate the settlement east of the forks of Turpentine Avenue with Bolongo Road and Redhook Road; other charts place it near the south shoulder of the ridge, and Reichel places it on Saltgut Cove immediately east.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nadirberg
description: Ridge about 330 feet high, with its summit about 750 yards north of the northern entrance to Mangrove Lagoon, St. Thomas.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nana Hill
description: Hill 347 feet high, about 985 yards northeast of Mosquito Bay in Southside Quarter, St. Thomas. The accepted spelling is Nana Hill, not Nanna.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nancy Hill
description: Conspicuous hill and the highest summit on the Eastend Peninsula of St. John, about 820 yards east of the Haulover. The triangulation station was named Eastend.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nancy's Hope
description: Estate comprising tract 36 in Queen Quarter and tract 8 in Company Quarter, St. Croix. Deeded to Joseph and Peter Robinson.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nanny Point
description: Eastern tip of a narrow salient ending in a steep jagged cliff about 40 feet high, surrounded by boulders, with a 52-foot knoll. It lies about 1,330 yards north-northeast of Ram Head and just north of Drunk Bay, southeastern St. John.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Narrow Bay
description: Bay fronting Betty's Hope and Montpellier or Cooper Bay estates, near longitude 64°48'45"W on the southern coast of St. Croix. The name appears to refer to the same feature as Cooper Bay or Negro Bay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Narrows
description: Generic term for the passage between Great Thatch Island and the northern shore of St. John. Also called The Narrows. The dictionary sometimes uses Thatch Narrows to avoid ambiguity with Thatch Island Cut.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nathanael Bay
description: Cove on the eastern side of Hurricane Hole, just north of Turner Point, St. John. The name appears on some charts as Nathaniel Bay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nattepan Bay
description: Cove about 110 yards west of Lucas Point, forming the western portion of Fortune Bay on the southern shore of St. Thomas. The name is Dutch and means clear pond; it is one of the earliest names and remained in local use.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Naval Station
description: United States Naval Station at St. Thomas, including quarters on the south side of Kongensgade east of the public park; naval building, radio station, marine barracks, ice plant, and related facilities around Fort Christian; Marine Quartermaster Department storehouse near Norregade and Generalgade; and navy-yard property on the southeast shore of Careening Cove, Hassel Island.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nazareth
description: Estate or mission on the crest of the isthmus between Vessup Bay and Nazareth Bay in Redhook Quarter, St. Thomas, overlooking Nazareth Bay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nazareth Bay
description: Bay 625 to 700 yards wide, west of Beverhout Point and northeast of Jersey Bay, on the south shore about 1.5 miles from the eastern end of St. Thomas.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Near Point
description: Point on the northwestern side of Hansen Bay, St. John, about 62 meters southeast of the triangulation point named Near.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Neck
description: Physiographic subdivision between the Western Oblong and Eastern Triangle of St. Croix, characterized by a break in the geological structure between the meridians of about 64°42'W and 64°46'W.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Negro Bay
description: Open bight on the southern coast of St. Croix. The Scorpion survey placed it at the south shore of Envy Estate, while later surveys placed it at Cooper Bay Estate. Also appears under several variant spellings and is closely associated with Cooper Bay and Narrow Bay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Negeru
description: Slave dungeon in the interior of the water fort, the outermost end of Fort Christian, St. Thomas City.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Negrobay
description: Estate comprising tract 46 and the western half of tract 47 in southeastern Prince Quarter, St. Croix. It was bounded north by Adventure, east by Golden Grove and Manning Bay, south by Envy, and west by Cooper Bay and Paradise. The name was formerly also applied to Manning Bay Estate.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Neltjeberg
description: Estate near a coconut grove southwest of Ruy Point and east of Turrel Bay in Little Northside Quarter on the northern shore of St. Thomas. The dictionary notes that Oldendorp placed Magens Plantage in this area.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Neltjeberg Hill
description: Hill overlooking Turrel Bay on the northern coast of St. Thomas. The Dutch name Neltjeberg means Nellie Hill.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: New Quarter
description: Quarter of St. Thomas embracing the central valleys from Bluebeard Hill about three miles east to Tutu Estate. It is bounded by Great Northside, Eastend, Redhook, and French Bay Quarters, St. Thomas Harbor, and the city. Van Keulen gave the alternative Dutch name Prince George's or New Quarter.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Newfound Bay
description: Indentation nearly 400 yards wide between coral reefs on the north shore of Eastend Peninsula, about half a mile northwest of Eastend Point, St. John. Local name. The Scorpion survey indicates it may be identical with Sibbe Bay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: New Herrnhut
description: Historic Moravian mission compound south of Tutu Road near the fork of Wintberg Road, about two miles east of St. Thomas City and about 1.5 miles east of Long Bay. It was an early center of the Moravian evangelistic movement in the Virgin Islands and included a notable cemetery for missionaries.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: New Love
description: Estate in Prince Quarter, St. Croix, also known as Die Liefde or Lower Love. It was associated with Old Love or Upper Love and the estate holdings of Lucas de Windt's heirs.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nicholas
description: Estate comprising tracts 34, 25, and 15, forming a block about 2,000 Danish feet wide and 6,500 Danish feet north-south, chiefly on a plateau over 700 feet above sea level. The mill was about 725 yards northeast of Mount Washington. Also spelled Nicolas and associated with Prospect Hill.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nisky
description: Moravian mission station and plantation at the northeastern foot of a 248-foot hill, along the south side of Mosquito Bay Road where it crosses the gap between hills west of Gregerie Bay, St. Thomas. The mission was founded in 1755 and preaching began there in 1763. Named for Niesky in Silesia.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Northside
description: Estate on the seacoast at the northwestern extremity of St. Croix, including tracts originally patented to Richard Richardson and Lieutenant Ripstorff. Sugar cane was cultivated in the northeastern portion; the remainder was largely bush. The village lay about one-quarter mile southwest of Ham Bay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Northside A Quarter
description: Rural district of St. Croix bounded east by Northside B Quarter, south by Westend and Prince Quarters, and north and west by the Caribbean Sea.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Northside B Quarter
description: Rural district of St. Croix conterminous on the south with Company, Queen, King, and Prince Quarters; bounded west by Northside A Quarter and north by the Caribbean Sea.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Northside Bay
description: Irregular crescent-shaped bight about four miles wide extending between Ham Bluff and Canebay Point along the shores of Northside A and Northside B Quarters, St. Croix.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Northside Bay
description: Older name for Magens Bay, St. Thomas. Variants include Dutch Noordzijde Baai, German Nordseite Bucht, French Baie du Nord, and Danish Nordside Bay or Store Nordside Bay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Northside Road
description: Road running northeast from Cruz Bay, skirting bays and crossing peninsulas around the north shore of St. John. Oxholm called it Nye Konge Vey, meaning New King's Road.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Northside Road
description: Road turning north from Centerline Road between Mount Pleasant and Plessen, then skirting Groveplace and traversing Upper Love, River, Parasol, and Prosperity to the north coast, and then east along the shore past Northstar, Canebay, Lavallee, Rustoptwist, and Baron Bluff to Salt River.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Northstar
description: Estate comprising tracts 19 and 20 in Northside B Quarter, southwest of Cane Bay on the northwest slope of Mount Eagle, St. Croix. The old mill tower and ruins stand near a deflection of the shore west of Cane Bay. Northstar and Prosperity were later merged with Canebay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nugent
description: Estate also called Castle Nugent, comprising tracts 41 and the southern half of 28, with the manse or estate house about half a mile from shore between Springs and Fareham Estates on the south coast of St. Croix.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nulliberg
description: Ridge forming the watershed between the valley of Charlotte Amalia Estate and New Herrnhut on the north and the southern shore of St. Thomas about one mile away. Nulliberg Ridge rises in two equally prominent summits of about 872 feet, one south of New Herrnhut and the other southeastward and north-northeast of Bolongo Estate.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nye Bay
description: Cove immediately north of Eastend, St. John. Oxholm's Nye Bay may be the same as Newfound Bay, though the dictionary notes some uncertainty about exact identification with nearby Sibbe Bay.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nye Konge Vey
description: Old Danish name meaning New King's Road, now known as Northside Road, St. John.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Nyhernhut
description: Danish spelling variants for New Herrnhut, the Moravian mission station east of Charlotte Amalie, St. Thomas.
source: Geographic Dictionary of the Virgin Islands

name: Maccumbo
description: Rocky, forest-covered hill in St. John; same as Makombi.

name: Madamberg
description: Hill north-northeast of Frederiksberg Point and east-southeast of Kiaer Tower. Danish form: Madambjerget.

name: Mafolie
description: Estate or plantation with residence on Mafolie Hill, north of St. Thomas Harbor. The name comes from French Ma Folie, meaning My Folly. Known for magnificent panoramic views and used by Danish astronomers in 1882 to observe the Transit of Venus.

name: Mafolie Hill
description: Hill on the crest of the main ridge of St. Thomas, commanding panoramic views of the city, harbor, Magens Bay, Culebra, Vieques, Sail Rock, St. Croix, St. John, Tortola, and surrounding cays.

name: Mafolie Road
description: Road connecting Lerkenlund and Louisehoi Roads east of Mafolie Estate. Known for steep ascent and superb views.

name: Magens-Pent
description: Original name of Cowell Point according to Høst; tied to the Magen family, one of the old island families.

name: Magen
description: Magens Plantage or Magen’s Estate, shown by Oldendorp at or near Neltjeberg.

name: Maho
description: Northside subdivision of St. John embracing the northern slope from Trunk Cay or Peter Beach eastward, touching Cruz Bay, Reef Bay, Coral Bay, and Eastend Quarters. Includes Whistling, Cinnamon, and Waterlemon Cays.

name: Maho Bay
description: Sheltered bay on the north shore of St. John between Maho Point and America Point, with a fine sand beach fringed with coconut palms. Named from the maho tree and historically called Little Maho Bay.

name: Mahobay
description: Estate with bay-oil still and banana grove on the eastern shore of Maho Bay.

name: Mahogany Road
description: Lane between Prosperity and Lagrange Estates, running east from the western shore to and through Lagrange Valley.

name: Maho Point
description: Tip of a short peninsula between Francis Bay and Maho Bay, formed by a spur of a 198-foot hill.

name: Maho Road
description: Road leaving Northside Road at Maho Bay, running east-southeast to the foot of a spur from King Hill, then ascending to Centerline Road.

name: Maho Track
description: Short cut from Maho Beach south to Old Works on Centerline Road at the junction with Reef Bay Road.

name: Mail Bay
description: Cove on the north coast of St. Thomas.

name: Maintop
description: Sailors’ name for Berg Hill, St. Thomas.

name: Makombi Peak
description: Rocky, forested summit in St. John reported as the local name of Camelberg. Described as over 1,200 feet high and covered with luxuriant forest, ferns, mosses, orchids, and other vegetation.

name: Malleville
description: Old estate southeast of Caret Bay and east-northeast of Pearl.

name: Mamey Garden
description: Place between Centerline Road and Mamey Peak, on the north slope of the peak.

name: Mamey Peak
description: Peak southeast of Maho Bay, just east of the fork of Centerline Road and Bordeaux Road, at a knot of mountain ridges. Named from the mammee or mamey apple tree.

name: Manchenil Bay
description: Bay at Diamond Keturah, east of Vagthus Point on the south coast of St. Croix. Named from the manchineel tree; first known as Anse de Galais.

name: Mandal
description: Estate, now in ruins, in Mandal Vale southwest of Mandal Bay.

name: Mandal
description: Estate on a 163-foot hill north of Kiddle Bay, on the south shore of St. John.

name: Mandal Bay
description: Bay with sand beach, mangrove clump, and salt pond west of Mandal Point. Named from old Mandal Estate.

name: Mandal Bay
description: Eligible alternative name of Grootpan Bay east of Cabrithorn Peninsula.

name: Mandal Hill
description: Knoll forming the summit of Mandal Point on the east side of Mandal Bay.

name: Mandal Point
description: Headland with cliffs 100 to 120 feet high, surmounted by Mandal Hill, projecting on the east side of Mandal Bay.

name: Mandal Point
description: Jagged bluff crowned by an 85-foot knoll on the west side of Kiddle Bay.

name: Mandal Road
description: Road from Mandal southeast to a point east of Peterson Hill, where it joins Tutu and Water Bay Roads.

name: Manglar
description: Spanish term for a clump of mangrove trees. A detached manglar occurs in Jersey Bay northwest of Rotto Cay and east of Compass Point.

name: Mangrove Lagoon
description: Shallow inlet enclosed on the east by Bovoni Cay, with boat channels at the north and south leading into the head of Jersey Bay.

name: Manning Bay
description: Estate in the southeast corner of Prince Quarter fronting Southside Road and the south coast. Named for original proprietor William Manning.

name: Maran
description: Widespread shrubby growth, especially in the dry Eastend hills of St. Croix. The term is associated with the Maran Hills and several Croton and Sida species.

name: Marché aux Cochons
description: French name meaning Hogmarket; a landing on the south coast of St. Croix, probably at King Bay, possibly Fairplain or Anguilla Bay.

name: Mardenboro Point
description: Wedgelike rocky salient extending southwest from the head of Hurricane Hole. Also known as Long Point or Mardenborough Point.

name: Punta Margal
description: Spanish name of Moor Point, meaning Marlpit.

name: Margaret Hill
description: Hill southeast of Durloe Bay in Cruz Bay Quarter, St. John.

name: Margarin
description: Seventeenth-century French estate at the present site of Christiansted.

name: Maria Cliff
description: South face of the headland between Calvary Bay and Chocolate Hole at the southwest extremity of St. John. Oxholm named the southwest point Maria Klip.

name: Maria Hill
description: Hill on the divide east of the road crossing from Bland to Petronella and Fareham, Eastend A Quarter.

name: Maria Hill
description: Estate 21, Eastend A Quarter. Oxholm’s map shows the tract subdivided into three north-south strips, with Endracht applied to the central strip.

name: Maria Bay
description: Name for Santa Maria Bay between Stumpy and Vluck Points, or for the south cove of the same.

name: Mariendal
description: Estate and school on the western slope of a 384-foot hill east of Turpentine Avenue and north of Mangrove Lagoon.

name: Marienhoi
description: Estate on the east side of the road from Southgate, near Great Pond. Site is now marked only by a well on Greatpond Estate.

name: Marine Barracks
description: Marine barracks near the northwest corner of Mosquito Bay; another Marine Barracks site noted at Gallows Bay, Christiansted.

name: Marlstone
description: Rock formation composed of carbonate of lime, forming the central slope of St. Croix.

name: Maronberg
description: Highest peak of Maroon Ridge, northwest of Springgarden Estate. Also called Maroon Hill or Ham Peak.

name: Maroon Hole
description: Bight in the cliff on the north coast west of Ham Bluff.

name: Maroon Ridge
description: Ridge from Annaly Gut to Ham Bluff. Its summit is Maronberg or Ham Peak.

name: Marsh
description: Estate house on Maho Bay toward the south end of the plain.

name: Mars Hill
description: Flat-topped eminence southeast of Frederiksted, St. Croix, on an estate of the same name.

name: Mars Hill
description: Estate 22 of Westend Quarter, originally called The Oval or Marshill. Later enlarged and united to Wheel-of-Fortune.

name: Martel
description: Seventeenth-century French estate near the cove later called Martel Bay.

name: Martel Bay
description: Old cove south-southwest of Shoy Point on the north coast of Eastend B Quarter, named from Martel Plantage on its east shore.

name: Martin
description: Early impermanent estate in Eastend A Quarter, marked by Oldendorp as the former Fr. Martin’s plantation.

name: Mary Bluff
description: Sea front of Mary Ridge, the most northerly shore of St. John, facing Thatch Narrows.

name: Mary Creek
description: Western cove of Leinster Bay, shut in by Mary Peninsula and entered by a narrow passage offering sheltered anchorage for small craft.

name: Mary Point
description: Western extremity of the peninsula forming the most northerly extension of St. John, a bold hammer-shaped headland. Also loosely used for Mary Peninsula.

name: Mary-Point Estate
description: Estate occupying the isthmus joining Mary Peninsula to the mainland of St. John, with landing at Mary Creek and banana and coconut groves along Francis Bay.

name: Mary Ridge
description: Triangulation station and summit of the peninsula ending at Mary Point.

name: Mary’s Fancy
description: Estate 16 and 17, Queen Quarter, originally William Davis’ Plantage, with ridges and estate buildings along the road following the crest of the western spur.

name: Mary’s Fancy
description: Estate 19 and 18a, John Thompson Plantage, Eastend B Quarter. Fan mill stood near the north shore at northwest corner of Cotton Valley.

name: Mary’s Point Bay
description: Local name for Francis Bay, St. John.

name: Mary’s Cap
description: Summit west-southwest of Bordeaux Mountain, St. John.

name: Masonic Point
description: Same as Annaberg Point, named because a large white Masonic Lodge building was long conspicuous to mariners entering Brim or Leinster Bay.

name: Mathias Tropaco Point
description: Dutch and French name for Tropaco Point on the north shore of St. Thomas.

name: Matthis Gut
description: Torrent bed in St. Thomas noted by Eggers.

name: Mauge
description: Seventeenth-century French estate not far from Canaan, St. Croix.

name: May Point
description: Triangulation station on the sharp bluff at the south end of Steven Cay, formerly known as Steven May.

name: Meeren Cay
description: Old name of Steven Cay in Pillsbury Sound. Shorter form: Meren; variants include Meeven and Mercy Key.

name: Menebek
description: Old estate north of Mosquito Bay and east of Brewers Bay, presumably named for a colonial family.

name: Mennebeck Bay
description: Bay on the northeast shore of Eastend Peninsula, probably a corruption of Menebek. Northwest entrance marked by Mennebeck or Menebek Point.

name: Merle Run
description: French Rivière Merle, a stream draining the valley in Slob, Barrenspot, and Jerusalem Estates and emptying into Grandfond or Limetree Bay. Merle means blackbird.

name: Meyer Bay
description: Shallow cove with a fine sand beach west of Lagoon Point.

name: Middle Passage
description: Channel between Thatch Cay and Grass Cay, leading from the Atlantic Ocean into Pillsbury Sound. Spanish name El Pasaje del Medio; local mariners call it Bull Hole.

name: Middle Point
description: Broad high neck between Princess Creek and Otter or Middle Creek in Hurricane Hole.

name: Midland
description: Estate on which Friedensfeld Moravian Mission and Midland Public School were located.

name: Midway Rock
description: Large detached shore rock off a rocky point midway between triangulation points Cocul and Long.

name: Miland
description: Place between America Hill and Maho Bay, at the south end of Maho Bay and foot of America Hill.

name: Miller
description: Estate in St. John. See Smithbay Estate.

name: Milord Point
description: West entrance of Great Pond Bay on the south coast of St. Croix; promontory of Fareham Hill. Bellin named it Cap du Milord.

name: Mingo Cay
description: Middle link in the chain with Grass Cay on the west and Lovango Cay on the east. Spanish alternative name Lovango Medio; also called Senior, Sinjo, and Singo.

name: Mingo Hill
description: Hill near the east end of Mingo Cay.

name: Mingo Point
description: Triangulation station on rounded bluff at the east end of Mingo Cay; the point itself lies farther north and west.

name: Mingo Rock
description: Breaker rock awash at low water west-southwest of Moravian Point, western extremity of St. John. Called Mingo Klippe by Oxholm.

name: Minna Hill
description: High, sharp, conspicuous peak overlooking Coral Bay, densely timbered with yellow and white sandalwood trees.

name: Mint
description: Estate 26b, adjoining Mountain Estate north of Centerline Road. Deeded to George Gasling and later named the Mint.

name: Mint Gut
description: Stream rising in Beck Grove or Allandale, flowing through Allandale, Hope, Mint, St. George, and Diamond to its confluence with St. George Beck.

name: Mirve
description: Seventeenth-century French plantation in the valley southwest of Gallows Bay.

name: Misgen
description: Estate near a 763-foot hill south of Magens Bay. Also spelled Misgunst.

name: Messiana Rest
description: Place on Centerline Road east-northeast of Mamey Peak.

name: Mr. Stalley’s Bay
description: Historic name for Stalley or Long Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Mizzentop
description: Sailors’ name for Kiaer, Government, or Blackbeard Hill.

name: Mohoe Bay
description: Variant spelling of Maho Bay.

name: Moir
description: Estate 30 and north half of 31, now Barrenspot, Queen Quarter. Associated with Alex Moir and Moir & Coakly holdings near Limetree Bay.

name: Molendal
description: Estate in Reef Bay Quarter, in the valley head north of Esperance Road, northwest of Genti Bay. Dutch name meaning Mill Valley.

name: Mohlenfels
description: Aberrant or variant spelling of Muhlenfels Point in old charts and Derrotero references.

name: Mon Bijou
description: Estate in King Quarter, originally belonging to Peter Heyliger Jr., later embracing tracts 8 and 9 and part of Blue Mountain slope. French name means my jewel. Site of Fredensfeld Mission.

name: Moncoeur
description: Seventeenth-century French plantation somewhere near Pearl Estate.

name: Monsieur du Bois, Gouverneur de l’Isle
description: Mansion of the French Governor of the Island on Governor Hill near St. John, St. Croix. M. du Bois had served for 12 years by 1676.

name: Montalvan
description: Spanish name of Saba Cay, appearing as La Isla de Montalván and El Islote de Montalván.

name: Montalvan Hill
description: Summit of Saba Cay, with a remarkable seaward cliff of hard cream-white and red felsite.

name: Montalvan Point
description: Southwest angle of Saba Cay at the foot of Montalvan Hill.

name: Montañas de Burdeos
description: Spanish name for Bordeaux Mountains, St. John.

name: Monte
description: Hamlet on a ridge north of Boatman Point, Rendezvous Bay. Below the bluff lies a rectangular north cove of Rendezvous Bay.

name: Montenac
description: Old estate shown by Oldendorp southeast of Caretbay Estate and east of Pearl, near Dorothea.

name: Montpellier
description: Estate in the northern tier of Prince Quarter, deeded to Ferrall Nugent, producing sugar cane and guavas.

name: Montpellier
description: Same as Dolby Hill Estate, St. Croix.

name: Montpellier
description: Name used on Hydrographic Office chart 1423 for Cooper Bay Estate.

name: Montpellier Mountain
description: Small estate of less than 60 acres, west half of tract 12, Prince Quarter, on Montpellier Mountain Ridge.

name: Montpellier Mountain
description: Ridge west of the upper course of Adventure Gut, southernmost spur of Bodkin Ridge.

name: Moor Point
description: Thin rocky salient forming the eastern side of Coral Bay entrance, thrusting out from the southern lobe of Eastend Peninsula.

name: Moravian Point
description: Peninsular salient between Frank Bay and Turner Bay, forming the westernmost extremity of St. John. Named for the Moravian Brethren, who began evangelization near this point.

name: More Hill
description: Prominent summit northeast of Hermitage Estate, east-southeast of Bryne Bay, and due north of the middle of Hurricane Hole entrance. Also called More’s Hill or Mount Pleasant.

name: Morgenstern
description: German name meaning Morningstar; alternative name for Henry Ryan’s Estate in Queen Quarter.

name: Morne Rond
description: French name meaning Round Hill, assigned in the seventeenth century to a conspicuous eminence at the eastern end of St. Croix, reported for a 380-foot hill near East Point.

name: Morningstar
description: Estate 9 and 4b in Queen Quarter, originally Henry Ryan’s Plantage. Also spelled Morning Star; German name Morgenstern.

name: Morningstar Bay
description: Bay on the southern shore of St. Thomas, stated to be the same as Soldier Bay.

name: Morro Hams
description: Spanish name of Ham Bluff. Also called Cabo del Diablo.

name: Mosquito Bay
description: Bay with fine sand beach between Cabritaberg and Grambokola promontories. The name likely originated as Musket Bay, from Danish troop gun practice, rather than mosquitoes.

name: Mosquito Bay
description: Estate occupying the extensive plain at the head of Mosquito Bay and fronting the road to the north.

name: Mosquito Bay Road
description: Southside turnpike from St. Thomas City west to Altona, Nisky, Mosquito Bay Estate, and nearby places.

name: Mosquito Point
description: South end of Grambokola Promontory, forming the most southerly extension of St. Thomas west of the harbor. Called Opper punt van Moschiete Bay by Van

name: Jacob de Koninks Punt
description: Early Dutch name of Konink Point, St. Thomas. The name is supposed to be a proper name, but may also be rendered as James the King or King James.

name: Ian de Muur
description: Plantage or estate northeast of Wintberg, at or near Mandal, St. Thomas.

name: Ian de Wints Plantagie
description: Old estate north or northwest of Jersey Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Ian Kramews Bay
description: Early Dutch name of Brewers Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Ianseb
description: Plantage, property of John Johnson, same as Munster Estate in Eastend A Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Iansens Plantage
description: Jansen Estate north-northeast of Tutu, St. Thomas.

name: Icaco Bay
description: Cocoplum, Plum, or Prune Bay east of Pull Point on the north coast of Eastend Quarter, St. Croix. Named from the plant Chrysobalanus icaco.

name: Ile Verte
description: French name properly referring to Green Cay, St. Croix, though transferred on some maps to Buck Island.

name: Indian Steen
description: Danish term for petroglyph.

name: Indian Inscription Point
description: Eastern extremity of Cam or Congo Cay, as named on the Scorpion survey.

name: Indsænkning
description: Danish term applied to the oceanic trough between Virgin Bank and St. Croix.

name: Inner Brass Island
description: Uninhabited island off the north shore of Little Northside Quarter, St. Thomas. Anchorage lies under the west side.

name: Ioannes Uytendaal Plantagie
description: Dutch name for Uitendal Estate, St. Thomas.

name: Ioannis Beuerout Punt
description: Early Dutch name of Beverhout Point, St. Thomas, confused by early cartographers with Deck Point.

name: Iohns Plantage
description: Old estate south of Magens Bay, or perhaps Hull Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Iohns Rest
description: Estate in Westend Quarter, St. Croix, originally McDonough Plantage and now Whim Estate.

name: Jonston Plantage
description: Johnston’s Glynn Estate, St. Croix.

name: Irvin
description: Either of two estates in Prince Quarter: Andreis Irvin’s Mount Pleasant or John Irvin’s Golden Grove.

name: Isaac Bay
description: Open bight between Point Cudejarre and Isaac Point on the south shore of Eastend Peninsula, St. Croix.

name: Isaac Point
description: Bend of bluff at the west side of Isaac Bay, southwest of East Point on the south coast of St. Croix.

name: Isaak de Klert Point
description: Probably identical with Water Point, and possibly the same as Cabrita Point. See notes on Redhook Point, Eastend, and Beverhout Point.

name: Isla Broken ó Buck
description: Spanish designation for Buck Island near St. Thomas.

name: Isla Chica de Hans Lollik
description: Spanish name of Little Hans-Lollik Island.

name: Isla del Agua
description: Spanish equivalent of Water Island.

name: Isla Grande de Hans Lollik
description: Spanish name of Great Hans-Lollik Island.

name: Isla Gras
description: Spanish name of Grass Cay.

name: Isle à Cabrit
description: French name for Buck Island, St. Croix. See Cabrits and Isle Vert.

name: Isle à Crabe ou Petit Isle de Saba
description: French name meaning Crab Island or Little Saba Island, an early name of Saba Cay.

name: Isle Bokken
description: Name for Buck Island.

name: Isle de l’Eau
description: French equivalent of Water Island.

name: Isle de Savaine
description: French name of Savana Island.

name: Isle du Sabbat
description: French name for Saba Cay.

name: Isle Hajje
description: French name of Shark Island.

name: Isle Plate
description: French name of Flat Cay.

name: Isle Rouge
description: French name of Rotto Cay.

name: Islea
description: Old estate east of Magens Bay, perhaps Lovenlund, St. Thomas.

name: Islet Rond et Birds Kay ou Caye des Oiseaux
description: French names for Frenchcap Cay.

name: Islote de Montalván
description: Spanish name of Saba Cay.

name: Ivers
description: Estate in the vicinity of Nana Hill, St. Thomas.

name: Jack Bay
description: Cove with pothook-shaped beach west of Adjett Point and extending to Hughes Point on the south shore of Eastend Peninsula.

name: Jack Rock
description: Largest rock in a cluster off the point separating Vessup Bay from Muller Bay.

name: Jacob Bay
description: Local name for Mennebeck Bay, or its southeast portion, in Eastend Quarter, St. John.

name: Jacob Flat
description: Small saucerlike plateau northeast of Minna Hill, Coral Bay Quarter.

name: Jacobins
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage somewhere near present Bonne Esperance, St. Croix.

name: Jacobsberg
description: Backbone ridge of the Christiansted Hills south of Christiansted, with highest summit at Signal Hill.

name: Jacobsberg
description: Estate situated on the north spur of Jacobsberg Ridge, at or near Lang’s Observatory and Eliza’s Retreat southeast of Christiansted Harbor.

name: Jacob’s Peak
description: Near Christiansted; either Signal Hill or Jacobsberg Ridge.

name: Jambi Bay
description: Variant of Jumbie Bay, from Bantu Njambi meaning spirit.

name: James Islands
description: Group composed of Great St. James, Little St. James, and Hunde or Dog Island.

name: Jansen
description: Old estate on St. Thomas shown on early maps as Iansens Plantage.

name: Jansen Point
description: Earlier name of Frederik Point, Hassel Island. Van Keulen named the area West Hoek and Daniel Jansen Punt.

name: Jasper Cove
description: Small rocky bight just east of Lucas Point, formerly called Jasper Point.

name: Jasper Point
description: Historic name of Lucas Point, named by the Dutch Jasper Jasperses Punt and by the French Pointe Jasper.

name: J. Bruce
description: Variant referring to John Brewer’s or John Bruce’s Bay. See Brewers Bay.

name: Jealousy
description: Estate in the east tier of Prince Quarter, patented to Wren Bagge. With Mount Pleasant and Glynn, it constituted Lucas’ sugar plantation.

name: Jealousy Gut
description: Stream also called Jealousy Bæk or Adventure Gut, rising on Big Fountain Estate and flowing southeast through several estates before joining Bethlehem or Kingshill Gut and becoming Fairplain Gut.

name: Jersey Bay
description: Large indentation between Deck Point and Patrick Point on the southeast coast of St. Thomas, partly enclosed by Cas Cay.

name: Jerusalem
description: Estate on the south coast of Queen Quarter, St. Croix, with mill tower north of Limetree Bay.

name: Jewel Cove
description: Present local name of Waterlemon Cay.

name: Jewfish Cove
description: Open bight northeast of Fortberg Peninsula on the west side of Hurricane Hole.

name: Jinny Gut
description: Deep mountain ravine east and south of Margaret Hill, near Bethany, dropping steeply and merging into Baas Gut.

name: Jinnygut Road
description: Road connecting Centerline Road with Sessman or Gift Hill Road.

name: Jochumdal
description: Estate near where Hammer Farm Road crosses the divide at the head of Guava Valley, south of Cinnamon Bay.

name: John Dunn
description: Estate between Contant and Solberg, near a hill where field sheets show a house just north of the hill.

name: John Needle’s Point
description: Same as Threadneedle Point.

name: Johnny-Hone Road
description: Road leaving Centerline Road at Emmaus, climbing a ravine near Base Hill, then descending to join Northside Road.

name: John Oley
description: Estate house near the southeast shore of Santa Maria or Tallard Bay on the north coast of St. Thomas.

name: John’s Folly
description: Estate occupying a hollow adjoining Johns Folly Bay in southeast St. John.

name: Johns Folly Bay
description: Bay between Sabbat Point and Nanny Point on the southeast shore of St. John, with coral reefs constricting the available entrance.

name: John Solomon Hill
description: Local name of Kaneel Hill, St. John.

name: Johnson Bay
description: Bay between Lagoon Point and Coral Harbor on the western side of Coral Bay, partly protected by Johnson Reef.

name: Johnson Reef
description: Coral reef from Freeze Bay to north of Lagoon Point on the western side of Coral Bay.

name: Johnson Reef
description: Coral formation off the northwest coast of St. John, midway between Durloe Cays and Whistling Cay. Spanish name Arrecife Johnson.

name: Jolly Hill
description: Estate in the north tier of Westend Quarter, deeded to John Jordan. Later joined to Little Grange as Logan Estate.

name: Jomfruøerne
description: Danish name of the Virgin Islands.

name: Joshee Gut
description: Streambed in St. John noted by Eggers.

name: Judge Berg’s Hill
description: Same as Berg Hill, named from Judge Berg’s large white residence near the summit, a conspicuous object for navigators entering St. Thomas Harbor.

name: Judge Berg’s Range Lights
description: Fixed red range lights on white towers on the east slope of Berg Hill, leading mid-channel into St. Thomas Harbor.

name: Judith Point
description: Salient at Judith’s Fancy Estate southeast of Salt River Point on the north coast of St. Croix.

name: Judith’s Fancy
description: Estate occupying Hemer Peninsula on the east side of Salt River Bay. Originally patented to Jens Peter Hemer and also called Hemers Plantage.

name: Jumbie Bay
description: Cove between Denis Bay and Trunk Bay with coral-sand beach and anchorage for small craft. The name derives from West African Bantu Njambi, meaning a supernatural being or spirit.

name: Jumbie Gut
description: Watercourse crossing French Bay Road and draining west-southwest to Soldier Bay on the south shore of St. Thomas.

name: Jungfernbank
description: German name of Virgin Bank.

name: Jungferninseln
description: German equivalent of Virgin Islands, also called Jungfernarchipel.

name: Jungferntiefe
description: German name meaning Virgin Deep.

name: Jurriaan Karstensis Huys
description: House on the central ridge south of Jurriaan Hansen or Hull Bay, somewhere near Signal Hill.

name: Kabritberg
description: Danish variant spelling of Cabritaberg.

name: Kakerlak
description: Danish equivalent of Cockroach Cay. Also spelled Kakkerlak or Kakelak, giving Creole Kakelaka.

name: Kalabasboom
description: Estate on Southside Road west of the beach at Freeze or Fryse Bay and northwest of Sabbat Point. Dutch name means calabash tree.

name: Kalksten Bay
description: Danish name of Limestone Bay.

name: Kalkun Cay
description: Rocky, steep, narrow bifid islet in Savana Passage west of St. Thomas. Creole and Danish Kalkun and Dutch Kalkoen mean turkey.

name: Kameelberg
description: Dutch name of Camelberg Peak.

name: Kaneel Bay
description: Dutch and Danish names for Cinnamon Bay.

name: Kaneel Hill
description: Hill south of Durloe Bay and east of Lind Point. From Dutch Kaneel and Danish Kanel meaning cinnamon. Local name in frequent use is John Solomon Hill.

name: Karantænestation
description: Danish variant of Quarantine Station in St. Thomas Harbor.

name: Karetbay
description: Danish form of Caret Bay, St. Thomas. Karette or Karetteskildpadde in Danish means loggerhead turtle.

name: Kaserne Hill
description: Same as King’s Hill, on which stands a casern or barracks in King Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Kasteel
description: Dutch name meaning castle, equivalent to Danish Kastel, applied by Van Keulen to Kastel Reef and Kastel Point.

name: Kastel Point
description: Bluff buttress resembling a round castle turret, with shore rock and reef, east of Vluck Point.

name: Kastel Reef
description: Reef off Kastel Point on the north shore of St. Thomas.

name: Katharinas Ryst
description: Danish name of Catherine’s Rest, St. Croix.

name: Kattegat
description: See Cattigut.

name: Kay Bay
description: Cay Bay, the westernmost portion of St. Thomas Harbor, east of Careen Hill.

name: K. C. Bay
description: Abbreviation of Klein Caneel or Klein Cinnamon, names of Durloe Bay. Pronounced and sometimes spelled Casey.

name: Kees Eyland
description: Early Dutch name of Cas Cay.

name: Kiaer Hill
description: Spur of ridge surmounted by Kiaer Tower, overlooking Fort Christian and St. Thomas Harbor. Also known as Government Hill and Blackbeard Hill.

name: Kiaer Shoal
description: Shoal in the middle of St. Thomas Harbor between Fort Christian and the coal wharf on Hassel Island.

name: Kiaer Tower
description: Stone tower on Kiaer Hill, built by Karl Baggert in 1674. Later known locally as Blackbeard Castle and formerly Fogarthy Castle.

name: Kiddle Bay
description: Cove between Kiddle Point and Mandal Point on the south shore of St. John. Early names include Mulat or Mulatte Bay and Little Mandal Bay.

name: Kiddle Point
description: Small peninsula ending in bluff between Kiddle Bay and Concordia Bay, northwest of Ram Head.

name: Kid Hill
description: Hill northwest of East Point, St. Croix, named from triangulation signal Kid.

name: Kid Rock
description: Small rock near the eastern shore of Capella Bay, south of the passage between the Capella Cays.

name: King
description: Estate on Centerline Road in King Quarter, formerly Heiliger Plantage and now named Upper Bethlehem on recent survey.

name: King Bay
description: Small indentation and landing on the south coast of St. Croix at or near the mouth of Fairplain Creek.

name: King Hill
description: Hill at the forks of Centerline, Maho, and Carolina Roads, St. John.

name: King Quarter
description: Quarter or ward of Charlotte Amalia or St. Thomas City.

name: King Quarter
description: Rural district of St. Croix bounded north by Northside B, east by Queen Quarter, west by Prince Quarter, and south by the Caribbean Sea.

name: King’s Hill
description: Kaserne Hill on which the casern or barracks stands in King Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Kingshill
description: Post office at the foot of King’s Hill on the south side of Centerline Road, between Frederiksted and Christiansted.

name: Kingshill Gut
description: Bethlehem Creek, one of the two largest watercourses of St. Croix, joining Jealousy Bæk to form Fairplain Creek.

name: Kingshill Range
description: Triangular uplift of limestone hills in King Quarter, including Kingshill Ridge and scattered hills eastward to Hope Estatehouse.

name: Kingshill Ridge
description: Ridge extending south from Kingshill Station to Southside Road at Fairplain, part of the Kingshill Range.

name: Kingshill Station
description: Barracks or casern on King’s Hill, St. Croix.

name: King’s Point
description: Point east of Caret Bay on the north shore of St. Thomas. Equivalent to Dutch Konink Point and distinct from Caret Point.

name: King’s Road
description: Turnpike following the straight line now called Centerline Road, St. Croix.

name: Muskitebay
description: Variant spelling of Mosquito Bay and Mosquito Bay Estate.

name: Museder
description: Seventeenth-century French estate near Annaly, St. Croix.

name: Musquite Bay
description: Variant spelling of Mosquito Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Musquitobay
description: Variant spelling of Mosquito Bay Estate on the north side of the road passing the bay.

name: Mud
description: Seventeenth-century French estate, probably on a 200-foot hill overlooking Cane Bay Estate.

name: Myrtle Mountain
description: Mountain southeast of Bordeaux Mountain and southwest of Sanders Bay, commanding a beautiful panorama in almost every direction.

name: La Caravelle
description: French name for Sail Rock in Virgin Passage, given by Bellin in Petit Atlas Maritime. English equivalent: The Caravel.

name: La Galiote
description: French name for Sail Rock in Virgin Passage. English equivalent: The Galliot or Bark.

name: Le Heu
description: French name for Sail Rock in Virgin Passage. English equivalent: The Hoy.

name: La Chapelle
description: French name meaning the Chapel, marked as an estate and apparently located on Jacobsberg Ridge.

name: La Chesnaye
description: Seventeenth-century French estate near Long Peak, St. Croix.

name: La Cucaracha
description: Spanish name of Turtledove Cay.

name: La Ensenada del Mosquito
description: Spanish name of Mosquito Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Lærkenlund
description: Danish form of Lerkenlund, interpreted as larch grove or more probably lark grove.

name: La Esperanza
description: Spanish equivalent of L’Esperance, St. John.

name: La Fleur
description: Old French estate about the northwest spur of Maria Hill, St. Croix.

name: La Forest
description: Seventeenth-century French estate near the northwest shore of Canegarden Bay, St. Croix.

name: El Islote Lagarto
description: Spanish name of Lizard Rock.

name: Laggard Hill
description: Spur of St. Thomas Ridge extending south toward Government Hill.

name: Lagoon Bank
description: Extensive shoal off the east shore of Christiansted Harbor southwest of Fort Louise Augusta.

name: Lagoon Point
description: Prominent salient on the western shore of Coral Bay, north of Sabbat Point. Also called Johnson Point.

name: Lagoon Mangrove
description: Several small mangrove clumps in the southeast portion of Mangrove Lagoon.

name: La Grande Princesse
description: French name of Grand Princess, later simply Princess, a large estate on the north coast of St. Croix.

name: La Granderie
description: Old French settlement near the north limits of Frederiksted, St. Croix.

name: La Grange
description: Large estate adjacent to Frederiksted on the east, extending along the west coast. Occupies a wide, well-watered plain planted in sugar cane, with estate village, great house, mill, and road to a wharf on Westend Bay.

name: Laguna del Manglar
description: Spanish name of Mangrove Lagoon, St. Thomas.

name: Lagune
description: Term referring to Altona Lagoon, also called Lagoon or The Lagoon.

name: La Isla Cabrito ó Savana
description: Spanish name of Savana Island.

name: Lakner’s Grab
description: German name marked on Oldendorp’s map between present Plessen and Diamond Estates, Prince Quarter, St. Croix.

name: La Masure
description: French form meaning the ruin or old shack, used as a mistaken etymology for Lameshur Estate.

name: Lamb Point
description: Name assigned by triangulation party to a bluff salient on Richard Smith’s Plantage northwest of East Point. Former French name was Pointe du Nordest.

name: Lambé Bay
description: French Anse des Lambis, same as Spring Bay, named from a kind of conch.

name: Lameshur
description: Estate with Moravian Mission school, bay-oil still, lime-juice still, landing, well, and wild bay and lime trees at the head of Little Lameshur Bay. The name signifies lemon-shore or lime-shore.

name: Lameshur Bay
description: Deep triple indentation on the south coast of St. John between White Point and Cabrithorn Point. Its east arm is Great Lameshur Bay, middle arm Little Lameshur Bay, and west cove Europa Bay.

name: Lameshur Bay
description: Name sometimes used for the easternmost and largest arm of Lameshur Bay, properly Great Lameshur Bay.

name: Lameshur Lagoon
description: Lagoon between Europa Bay and Billington Hill, Reef Bay Quarter, St. John.

name: Lameshur Road
description: Road leaving Reef Bay Road in Parforce Valley, climbing Buonavista Hill, crossing a col, and descending to Lameshur.

name: Lammert Bay
description: Original name of Dorothea Bay on the north shore of St. Thomas.

name: Lammert Point
description: Early Dutch and Danish name of Dorothea Point, St. Thomas.

name: Lang Bank
description: Hook-shaped wall-sided coral ledge extending east from Buck Island and northeast of East Point, St. Croix.

name: Lang-Bay
description: Danish or Dutch form referring to Long Bay in St. Thomas Harbor.

name: Lang Bay
description: Bight south of Pelican Rock in the southeastern part of Round Bay, St. John. Englished as Long Bay by H.M.S. Scorpion.

name: Lange-Rev
description: Danish name of Long Reef, Christiansted Harbor.

name: Langford
description: Variant spelling of Longford Estate, Company Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Langmath
description: Estate at the end of a trail branching east from Turpentine Avenue, same as Longmat.

name: Lang Peak
description: Peak on Carina Mountain southeast of Lang’s Observatory, named for the Lang family.

name: Lang Point
description: Danish descriptive name for Cottongarden Point.

name: Lang Pynt
description: Danish name for Long Point or Point Espagnole on the south coast of St. Croix.

name: Langpynt Bay
description: Danish equivalent of Longpoint Bay, St. Croix. See Ruan Bay.

name: Lang Ridge
description: Spur extending northwest from Lang Peak on Carina Ridge. Ruins of Eliza’s Retreat and Lang’s Observatory lie on the ridge.

name: Lang’s Centerveien
description: Roadway in St. Croix noted by Eggers.

name: Lang’s Observatory
description: Observatory on a hill at the northern end of Lang Ridge, east of Christiansted.

name: La Piedra del Scorpion ó Alacrán
description: Spanish name of Scorpion Rock.

name: La Piedra Kiaer
description: Spanish name corresponding to Kjærs Klippe or Kiaer Shoal.

name: Laprey Valley
description: Small plain enclosed by hills in tract 26, Eastend A Quarter, St. Croix.

name: La Princesa
description: Spanish name of Princess Estate, St. Croix. Also called La Princesa Grande.

name: La Princesse
description: Public school at Princess Estate, St. Croix; the French name was also used for the estate.

name: La Providence
description: Alternative or parenthetic name for Water Island, from a plantation whose name remains on Providence Point.

name: La Bahia del Sudoeste
description: Spanish name of Southwest Road.

name: La Roca de Hans-Lollik
description: Spanish name of Hans-Lollik Rock.

name: La Reine
description: Estate comprising tract 20 in King Quarter with 10b in Queen Quarter north of Centerline Road. The French name means the Queen.

name: Lareine Hill
description: Hill at the southern end of a ridge around which Centerline Road makes a detour, south of Lareine Estate.

name: La Roca Caravela
description: Spanish name meaning Caravel Rock, same as Sail Rock.

name: La Rouche
description: Seventeenth-century French estate on a hill west of Sugar Bay, St. Croix. Possibly should read La Bouche, meaning the mouth of Salt River.

name: La Taille
description: Old estate on a hill forming a point on the northeast shore of Altona Lagoon near Shoy.

name: La Walvgst
description: Goodhope or Bonne Esperance Estate, Queen Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Lavango Cay
description: Variant spelling of Lovango Cay.

name: La Vallée
description: Moravian mission and estate, same as Lavallee, St. Croix.

name: Lavallee
description: Estate in Northside B Quarter, formerly William Pickering Plantage. French name means the valley. Seat of a Moravian mission and associated with the bay called Grand Cannebay on old French maps and Little Cane Bay on H.O. 1423.

name: Lavielle Bay
description: Same as Anse à la Vieille, on the estate of Robert Stewart. A gut or crush runs back to the north break of Bodkin Ridge.

name: Lazaretto
description: Old designation of the quarantine reservation at Muhlenfels Point, St. Thomas, later taken over and improved by the United States Government.

name: Lebanon
description: Estate at the north edge of the Central Plain, southwest foot of the Salt River Hills, part of original holdings of Baron de Breton.

name: Lebanon Gut
description: Stream tributary to Concordia Creek and the valley watered by the stream, also called Lebanon Hill Gut.

name: Lebanon Hill
description: Hill north of Lebanon Mill on Lebanon Estate, St. Croix.

name: Le Bassin
description: Early French name of Christiansted Harbor. The town retained the colloquial name Bassin.

name: Leduck Cay
description: Islet at Coral Bay entrance, midway between Moor Point and Ram Head. Named by Gerard van Keulen as Peter le Duck’s Eyland, likely for a Flemish colonial. Later called Duck Island and Buck Island; present name distinguishes it from other Buck Islands.

name: Leeger Punt
description: Red Point, St. Thomas, named on Van Keulen’s map as Leeger Punt van Moschiete Bay.

name: Lee Hill
description: Triangulation station on Mafolie Ridge, north of St. Thomas Harbor and south of Magens Bay, with commanding views of both.

name: Lee Point
description: Western extremity of the rocky peninsula forming the westernmost projection of Thatch Cay.

name: Lee Rock
description: Rock close to Lee Point at the western extremity of Thatch Cay.

name: Leeward Passage
description: Safe passage between Thatch Cay and the north shore of St. Thomas.

name: Le Hoy
description: French name meaning the Hoy, an alternate name of Sail Rock.

name: Leinster Bay
description: Double indentation on the north shore of St. John, forking into Mary Creek on the west and Waterlemon Bay on the southeast. Formerly called Brim Bay.

name: Leinster Bay
description: Estate with cattle ranch and reform school at the eastern end of Leinster Bay, likely identical with Waterlemon Cay Estate.

name: Leinster Hill
description: Hill near Threadneedle Point on the north coast of St. John.

name: Leinster Point
description: Cuspidate rock east of Leinster Bay on the north shore of St. John.

name: Lemon Tree Bay
description: Same as Limetree Bay, St. Croix.

name: Leper Asylum
description: Group of buildings near the western shore of Christiansted Harbor at a double rounded point.

name: Le Poids
description: Seventeenth-century French estate on the site of Little Princess, St. Croix.

name: Lerk
description: Two old estates not far from Solberg, St. Thomas.

name: Lerken Bay
description: Small bight on the southwestern shore of Magens Bay, northeast of Lerkenlund Hill and Estate.

name: Lerkenlund
description: Estate on Lerkenlund Hill overlooking Magens Bay. Danish name derived from lark and grove, hence Larkgrove; corrupted in Creole into Let-alone.

name: Lerkenlund Hill
description: Bench on the north slope northeast of Signal Hill in Great Northside Quarter, St. Thomas.

name: Lerkenlund Road
description: Road joining Dorothea and Solberg Roads at a col, then running north, east to Lerkenlund, and southeast to the Misgen fork.

name: L’Escallus
description: Seventeenth-century French estate near Springgut Notch, St. Croix.

name: Lesle
description: Old French estate on a spur of hills west of the road south of Mount Welcome and Gallows Bay.

name: L’Esperance
description: Estate on St. John, same as Esperance.

name: L’Esperance
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage near present Two Brothers Estate, St. Croix.

name: Lestan Bay
description: Same as Anse de Lestan, St. Croix.

name: LeVert
description: Seventeenth-century French estate near present Camporico, St. Croix.

name: Libanon
description: Original spelling of Lebanon Estate, St. Croix.

name: Lieven Point
description: Same as Sabat or Sabbat Point, St. John.

name: Liever Marches Bay
description: Small bight east of Brown or Bryne Bay on the north shore of St. John. Possibly from French Marché des Lievres, meaning Hare-market.

name: Liliendal
description: Ravine or gut descending from Liliendal Col to Dorothea Bay. Danish name from lily and dale, meaning Lilyvale or Lilydell.

name: Liliendal
description: Estate west of Signal Hill, identified with Brown Estate by comparison of old maps and later field sheets.

name: Liliendal Col
description: Saddle on the main ridge at the head of Liliendal Gut, where roads fork toward Solberg, Resolution, and Lerkenlund.

name: Lilienschild
description: Old estate near the ridge crest in the vicinity of Resolution, St. Thomas.

name: Lille Cane Bay
description: Danish name of Little Cane Bay, St. Croix.

name: Lille Cruzbay
description: Danish name meaning Little Cross Bay, now Cruz Bay.

name: Lille Hanslollik
description: Danish name of Little Hans-Lollik Island.

name: Lille James Eyland
description: Name compounded from Danish Lille, English James, and Dutch Eyland, referring to Little St. James Island.

name: Lille Kanel Bay
description: Danish equivalent of Little Cinnamon Bay, same as Durloe Bay.

name: Lille Krum Bay
description: Danish name of Little Krum Bay.

name: Lille Maho Bay
description: Danish name meaning Little Maho Bay, now simply Maho Bay.

name: Lille Middelgrund
description: Danish name of Little Middleground in Christiansted Harbor.

name: Lille Mount-Pleasant Bæk
description: Danish name meaning Little Mount-Pleasant Beck or Gut, a stream on Little Mount Pleasant Estate.

name: Lille Nordside Bay
description: Danish equivalent of Little Northside Bay, same as Hull Bay.

name: Lille-Norge
description: Estate among hills northeast of Mariendal, St. Thomas. Danish name means Little Norway.

name: Lille Saba
description: Danish name of Saba Cay or Little Saba Island.

name: Lille St. Thomas Bay
description: Danish name of Little St. Thomas Bay.

name: Limeshore
description: English equivalent of Lameshur, St. John.

name: Limestone Bay
description: Bay on the northern side of Carol Point, indenting the middle of the southeast shore of Water Island. Danish name Kalksten Bay.

name: Limestone Rock
description: Outer and smaller of twin rocks on an extensive coral reef south of Carol Point, Water Island.

name: Limetree
description: Estate in western Queen Quarter, deeded to Isaac Hartman and also called Hartmann. Mostly sugar plantation.

name: Limetree Bay
description: Semicircular indentation south of Jerusalem Estate on the south coast of St. Croix, with good anchorage in the center.

name: Limetree Cove
description: Tiny bay with beach and well on the north side of Round Bay between Hansen Bay and the Haulover, Eastend Peninsula, St. John.

name: Lind Point
description: North tip of the projection north of Cruz Bay on the west shore of St. John. Probably from Dutch Linde, meaning limetree.

name: Lindqvist
description: Farm at Denis Bay, St. John.

name: Lisenland
description: Valley between Havensight and Bellevue, St. Thomas.

name: Lisenlund
description: Estatehouse on the summit of Lisenlund or Bellevue Hill, overlooking St. Thomas Harbor.

name: Lisenlund Hill
description: Hill south-southeast of Havensight Hill and near Muhlenfels Point. Also called Bellevue Hill.

name: Little Cane Bay
description: Open bight washing the shores of Lavallee and Rustoptwist Estates in Northside B Quarter. Early French maps call it Grand Cannebay.

name: Little Cinnamon Bay
description: Alternative name of Durloe Bay.

name: Little Cockroach
description: Name for Cricket Rock.

name: Little Coculus Bay
description: Cove east of Green Cay and west of Coculus Point on the south shore of St. Thomas.

name: Little Cruz Bay
description: Now designated simply as Cruz Bay. The name was used to distinguish it from Great Cruz Bay, now Calvary Bay.

name: Little Current Hole
description: Boat passage between Little St. Thomas and a 42-foot islet.

name: Little Diamond
description: Diamond Keturah Estate and Mill in Company Quarter, St. Croix.

name: Little Flat Cay
description: Bare rock northeast of Big Flat Cay. Spanish equivalent Rasito; called Vogel Eyland by Van Keulen.

name: Little Fountain
description: Estate in northern King Quarter, also called Fountain. Later merged with Mon Bijou.

name: Little Fountain
description: Estate 13, Testman Plantage, Northside B Quarter, St. Croix. Also called Mount Pleasant.

name: Little Grange
description: Estate in Mahogany Valley northeast of Frederiksted, with grassy ridges north and south and an extensive banana field. Also called Little La Grange.

name: Little Green Key
description: Same as Green Cay, St. Croix.

name: Little Hans-Lollik
description: Island north of Hans-Lollik, joined to it by a coral ledge. Other names are translations in Danish, Spanish, and German.

name: Little Krum Bay
description: Cove containing a wreck, north-northeast of Regis Point on the south shore of St. Thomas.

name: Little Lameshur Bay
description: Middle of the three principal arms of Lameshur Bay, with good anchorage, common sailboat use, and a sand beach.

name: Little Maho Bay
description: Older name for present Maho Bay, used to distinguish it from Great Maho Bay, obsolete name of Mary Creek.

name: Little Mandal Bay
description: Name given on C. & G. S. field sheet T. 3783 to Kiddle Bay, St. John.

name: Little Middleground
description: Small shoal northwest of Lagoon Bank, north-northeast of Protestant Cay in Christiansted Harbor.

name: Little Norge
description: Estate among hills northeast of Mariendal. Danish Lille-Norge means Little Norway.

name: Little Northside
description: Quarter of St. Thomas bounded by watersheds from Vluck Point to Crown Mountain, Signal Hill, and Dorothea Point, including the Brass Islands.

name: Little Plantation
description: Estate in St. John noted by Eggers.

name: Little Princess
description: Estate in Company Quarter with house, mill, settlement, and landing at the western extremity of Christiansted Harbor. Combined with Golden Rock as Phillips’ Sugar Estates.

name: Little Saba
description: Name for Saba or Montalvan Cay, used to distinguish it from Saba Island.

name: Little Saint James
description: Island south-southeast of Great St. James Island. Variant names include Klyn St. Jems, Petit St. James, Lille James Eyland, and Santiago Chico.

name: Little St. Thomas
description: Low grassy peninsula, almost an islet, joined by a tombolo to the west end of St. Thomas.

name: Little St. Thomas Bay
description: Small gravelly cove on the south shore of the west end of St. Thomas just south of Little St. Thomas, used by small boats when the sea is rough at Sandy Bay or Botany Bay.

name: Living Gut
description: Small sparkling brook draining the ravine east of Rustenberg and Camelberg, forming a cascade and pool at the southern foot of Doubloon Hill where Carib inscriptions are found.

name: Lizard Rock
description: Steep rugged islet west of Inner Brass Island and north of Vluck Point, St. Thomas.

name: Lizard Rocks
description: Group of six bare rocks, the largest called Lizard or Lagarto Rock, with rocks awash westward called Blenders.

name: Lizard
description: Erroneous name for Cockroach Cay. Lizard Rock is a different islet southeast of Cockroach Cay.

name: Loango
description: Variant of Lovango Cay. Name refers to Loango, a district on the west coast of Africa north of the Congo River.

name: Loisa Augusta
description: Variant spelling of Louise Augusta, in whose honor Fort Louise Augusta east of Christiansted was named.

name: Lodsø
description: Danish alternative name of Protestant Cay.

name: Lollik Hill
description: Summit of Hans-Lollik Island, described in the Derrotero as Peñon Escarpado, a rugged crag.

name: Lomo Tortuga
description: Spanish name of Turtleback Rock.

name: Long Bay
description: East cove of St. Thomas Harbor. Southeast shore formed by West-India Dock; northeast shore called Long Bay Beach.

name: Long Bay
description: Common name of Stalley Bay on the south shore of St. Thomas.

name: Longford
description: Large estate occupying the southeast portion of Company Quarter, composed of several former plantages and the shore of Spring Bay.

name: Longmat
description: Estate south of a 516-foot hill, same as Langmath.

name: Long Point
description: Most southerly extremity of St. Thomas, terminus of a ridge on a peninsula west of Mangrove Lagoon. Originally named Stalley Point.

name: Long Point
description: Low grassy salient on the south coast of St. Croix at the southeast corner of Westend Quarter. French name Pointe Espagnole; Danish Lang Pynt or Langpynten.

name: Long Point
description: Common name of Mardenboro Point, St. John.

name: Long Point Bay
description: Chart name of Longpoint or Ruan Bay on the south coast of St. Croix.

name: Long Reef
description: Reef off the southern shore of St. Croix opposite Krause Point, enclosing a good anchorage.

name: Long Reef
description: Narrow bar stretching from Princess Plain eastward, enclosing the western side of Christiansted Harbor entrance.

name: Loots Kay
description: Obsolete Dutch name of Protestant Cay. Properly Loods Kay, from loods meaning pilot.

name: Lorenz
description: Old estate northwest of St. Thomas Harbor and southeast of Solberg.

name: Los Dos Santiagos
description: Spanish name meaning The Two Saints James, referring to the St. James Islands.

name: Los Triángulos
description: Spanish name meaning The Triangles, or Triangle Rocks.

name: Louisehoi
description: Estate and country house on the main ridge between Magens Bay and St. Thomas Harbor, commanding views of both. Name combines Louise with Danish høi/høj, meaning height.

name: Lovango Cay
description: Island northwest of Hognest Point, St. John, separated from Mingo Cay by a shoal passage. The name derives from Loango, a district on the west coast of Africa.

name: Lovango Cays
description: Three islands administratively attached to Cruz Bay Quarter: Lovango, Congo, and Mingo Cays.

name: Lovango Chico
description: Spanish name for Congo Cay, meaning Little Lovango.

name: Lovango Grande
description: Spanish name meaning Great Lovango, same as Lovango Cay.

name: Lovango Hill
description: Hill and triangulation station on the eastern end of Lovango Cay.

name: Lovango Medio
description: Spanish name for Mingo Cay, meaning Middle Lovango.

name: Love Gut
description: Partly dry watercourse rising in River Estate, flowing through Upper and Lower Love, and discharging into Jealousy Gut.

name: Lovenlund
description: Estate east-southeast of Magens Bay, St. Thomas.

name: Lovenlund Bay
description: Rocky cove on the north shore of Great Northside Quarter, north of Lovenlund Estate.

name: Lower Love
description: Estate in Prince Quarter. With Upper Love it was patrimony of Lucas de Windt’s heirs. Formerly also called New Love or Die Liefde.

name: Lowry Hill
description: Estate in Eastend A Quarter, west side of the road to Petronella, named from George Lowry, proprietor. Later one of the Arnesen Estates.

name: Lucas Point
description: Rounding rocky salient of the steep south shore of Westend Quarter on the east side of Fortune Bay. Earlier Dutch and French names include Jasper Jasperses Punt and Pointe Jasper.

name: Luckett Hill
description: Same as Bluebeard Hill, St. Thomas.

name: Lysthus
description: Pleasure house and prominent object on the top of Careen Hill, St. Thomas.

name: Oiseaux, Caye des
description: French for “Cay of the Birds” or “Bird Cay,” equivalent to Dutch “Vogelklip.” The name was applied to rocky islets used as nesting places by seabirds, including Frenchcap Cay and Grass Cay.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Økæde
description: Danish term meaning “island-chain,” used for chains of cays such as Thatch, Grass, Mingo, and Lovango north of St. John.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Old Love
description: Former name of Upper Love Estate, comprising estates 18 and 19 in Prince Quarter, St. Croix.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Old Pye
description: Estate fronting the southern side of Centerline Road along the western border of Prince Quarter. It included tract 40, formerly Waterground Estate, plus tracts 41a and 41b, the latter formerly William’s Delight. In 1856 it was combined with Bog-of-Allen as Bushby plantation.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Old Ruins
description: General designation for vestiges of abandoned plantations, including ruins on a 68-foot knoll southwest of Mount Pleasant near the mapped location of Smithbay Estate, and ruins on a 316-foot hill east-southeast of Tutu.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Ole Bay
description: Inner cove of Santa Maria Bay near John Oley Estate on St. Thomas.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: John Oley
description: Estate at the southeastern bend of Santa Maria Bay, giving rise to the local names Ole Bay or Oley Bay.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oostende
description: Dutch equivalent of Eastend, the sixth quarter of St. John, comprising the Eastend Peninsula east of the meridian through More Hill. Oxholm’s 1780 map listed seven estates in this quarter.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oostende Quarters A and B
description: Dutch/Danish form of Eastend A and Eastend B Quarters, St. Croix.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oostent Bay
description: Early Dutch name for the bay shown by Van Keulen southeast of Coki Point. It likely refers to Water Bay and perhaps Smith Bay, east of St. Thomas.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oostent Punt
description: Dutch name meaning “Eastend Point.” Early maps applied it to the most prominent salient between Coki Point and Redhook Point. Usage became confused through similar coastal configurations; it is now associated with Cabes Point rather than the more literal Redhook Point.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oost Hoek
description: Dutch for “East Hook,” applied to Pacquereau Point, now Muhlenfels Point, at the east side of St. Thomas Harbor entrance.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oost Wal
description: Dutch for “East Bank,” applied by Van Keulen to the shore of St. Thomas Harbor north of Pacquereau/Muhlenfels Point.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Opper Punt
description: Dutch phrase meaning “upper point of Mosquito Bay,” now Mosquito Point on St. Thomas.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Orangegrove
description: Estate spanning adjacent tracts in the northwestern corner of Prince Quarter and northeastern corner of Westend Quarter. Guavas grew wild, and a considerable village stood in the valley.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Orangegrove
description: Estate in Company Quarter, about three-quarters of a mile from the northern coast west of Christiansted. It was the old Saple Plantage with later boundary changes toward Aldershville.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Orangegrove Road
description: Road nearly one mile long connecting Annaly and Orangegrove Estates.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Orkanhul
description: Danish name meaning “Hurricane Hole,” referring to Hurricane Hole on St. John. Older charts spell it Orcan Hul or Orcan-Hullet.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Orkaans Gat
description: Early Dutch/Danish/German name for Careening Cove on Hassel Island, St. Thomas Harbor, meaning hurricane inlet or hole.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Ornen Rock
description: Sunken navigation danger with a shoal depth of about 9 feet, one mile east of Inner Brass Island and half a mile northwest of Picara Point. Danish Ørnen means “the Eagle.”
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Østende
description: Danish/Dutch name meaning “Eastend,” applied to East Point, St. Croix.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Ostende Bay
description: Bay about 660 yards wide between East Point and Point Cudejarre, with a straight 320-yard beach on Eastend B Peninsula, St. Croix.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Otter Creek
description: Cove in the northeastern portion of Hurricane Hole, between Princess Bay and Water Creek, St. John.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Outer Brass Island
description: Island north of St. Thomas, 412 feet high, about 1,400 yards long and 720 yards wide, with an area of about 108 acres, excluding Grasklip Cay. It is overgrown with palms and brush.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oval
description: Former estate in the northern half of tract 22, Westend Quarter, later merged into Mars Hill Estate.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Overhale
description: Danish name meaning “Overhaul” or “Haulover,” applied to the portage across the narrow isthmus of Eastend Peninsula, St. John.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oxford
description: Estate comprising tracts 5 and 6 in the southern tier of Northside A Quarter. Its estate house stood in a picturesque valley-head; it was later associated with the Rustoptwist/Northrope estate holdings.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oxford Hill
description: Hogback ridge about 623 feet high extending from the northeastern part of Oxford Estate toward Annaly, Northside A Quarter.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oxford Road
description: Road leaving Mahogany Road at Jolly Hill Estate, ascending Oxford Gut and crossing hills north-northeast to Annaly.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Oyen Hill
description: Hill about 357 feet high between Reef Bay and Fish Bay, St. John. Oxholm called it Oyens Bjerg.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Packet Rock
description: Coral reef about 100 yards in extent with least depth around 5 feet, located north of Buck Island and off the south coast of St. Thomas.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pacquereau Bay
description: Bay about 700 yards wide on the east side of St. Thomas Harbor entrance, north of Muhlenfels Point, formerly Pacquereau Point.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pacquereau Point
description: Original name of Muhlenfels Point on the east side of St. Thomas Harbor entrance, likely from a Huguenot colonial family. Danish spelling became Pakero and later the corrupted Pokro.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pas-Perdu
description: French name meaning “lost land,” applied to the mangrove-island/point enclosing Krause Lagoon on the south coast of St. Croix.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Palestina
description: Settlement or estate westward of Popilleau Bay on Hurricane Hole, St. John.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Paletuvier
description: French name for the black mangrove, Avicennia nitida, growing in shallow water and lagoon mud. The term appears in the old name Anse des Partuviers for Tague Bay.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pan Bay
description: Open bight in the western part of Round Bay, near Turner Point, St. John. The name refers to a small pond behind the beach.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pannet
description: Name of two early estates in St. Thomas: one midway between Wintberg and Magens Bay, and another west-northwest of Wintberg and east of Lerkenlund.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pantaleon
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage situated on Kirkegaard Hill, west of Sugar Bay, St. Croix.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Paquerau
description: Estate and mill shown on Oxholm’s map of St. John near the 1,099-foot summit south of Mamey Peak and east of Reef Bay Road. The name may be related to Pacquereau in St. Thomas.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Paradeground
description: Open space east of Christiansted, St. Croix. Danish name: Paradepladsen.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Paradise
description: Estate comprising the northern halves of tracts 44 and 45 in Prince Quarter. Its mill stood on the southern foot of Mount Pleasant. It was later merged with Adventure.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Parasol
description: Estate 16 in Northside B Quarter, with a 747-foot peak near the center and road from River to Prosperity along the western slope. It was a stockfarm attached to Fountain.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Parasol Hill
description: Ridge extending southeast from the 747-foot peak on Parasol Estate, near the Northside watershed.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Parforce
description: Estate occupying a plain at the south end of the valley opening onto northeast Reef Bay, St. John. It is identified with Reefbay Estate.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Parhien
description: Seventeenth-century French plantage near the present site of Petronella Estate, St. Croix.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Partuvier Bay
description: Old French name for Tague or Take Bay on the northern coast of Eastend, St. Croix.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Paso de la Isla Buck
description: Spanish name for Buck Island Pass or Channel, St. Croix. The deeper portion was called “Fondeadero al Sudoeste de la Isla Buck.”
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pasaje de la Isla Cabrito
description: Spanish name for Savana Passage.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pasaje del Medio
description: Spanish name for Middle Passage.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pasaje de Sotavento
description: Spanish name for Leeward Passage west and south of Thatch Cay.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Paso Consejos
description: Spanish name for Flanagan Passage, meaning “Council Pass.”
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Patience
description: Old estate comprising the east half of tract 35 in Prince Quarter, later part of Adventure Estate.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Patricia Cay
description: Cay about three-quarters of a mile long, mostly mangrove swamp, immediately south of Bovoni Cay, ending in Patrick Point.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Patrick Point
description: Salient at the southeastern end of Patricia Cay, marked by a 75-foot knoll on the southern side of St. Thomas.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pearl
description: Estate on the main ridge of St. Thomas, northwest of Crown Mountain, between Zambee and Bonne Esperance.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section

name: Pearl
description: Estate comprising tracts 38, 43, and 44 in Queen Quarter, southwest of the intersection of Southside and Canegarden Roads, with a strip to Canegarden Bay. It was Abraham Heyliger’s Plantage.
source: Virgin Islands Geographic Dictionary, O–P section
